parts.text:
The current sidecar chat's MCP tools operate on sidecar DB. To keep local-first, local orchestrator is the way. But maybe we can keep sidecar chat as an "enhanced mode" that uses local data by proxying tool calls to the browser? That's not possible without WebSocket/RPC from sidecar to browser. We could have the browser expose a local tool execution endpoint via a Service Worker? Sidecar can't reach browser. So local orchestrator is required.

Scope of local orchestrator: The existing Python chat tool loop is ~350 lines. Porting to TS is feasible. Tool definitions for MCP/core can be generated. We can reuse the UI catalog and protocol already in TS. The local tools are straightforward. External tools (connectors/MCP) can be discovered/executed through new sidecar endpoints; but the core MCP tools shouldn't be forwarded because they'd hit sidecar DB. We can filter them out by name: core tool names handled locally; unknown tools forwarded to sidecar.

But the sidecar's MCP server exposes core tool names. If the local orchestrator forwards a core tool by mistake, data divergence. We can maintain a `LOCAL_TOOL_NAMES` set and always handle them locally; external tools are any other names. Also the sidecar can expose `GET /api/tools` returning all MCP tools; local filters. Connectors aren't MCP tools; the sidecar's chat currently uses `add_connector` local tool and MCP tools. Connector invocation isn't in chat.py! It only lists/registers connectors; the actual ingest is via CLI/MCP connector package. So "connectors" enhanced capability is mostly management, not chat tool invocation. Fine. Sidecar `/api/connectors` already exists and can remain sidecar-only.

MCP external tools: The MCP server in this repo is the ODI data server; no external MCP tools are loaded into the chat. `mcp_tools` comes from `request.mcp_url` (the ODI MCP server) and includes core tools. So there are no extra external tools in the current chat. The "MCP" enhancement is really the sidecar's tool loop over the same core data. In local-first, we replace that with local tools. Connectors are managed but not invoked in chat. So the enhanced sidecar capabilities are:
- Server-side LLM proxy (CORS/key hiding).
- Server-side memory/conversations (but user wants local memory/history; we can still use local).
- Connector registry management/health (sidecar-only filesystem integration).
- MCP server integration/CLI parity (not user-facing chat).
- Possibly richer UI surfaces? UI rendering is local.
Thus, local-first chat can fully replicate the chat tool loop for core tools. The sidecar enhancement is mainly LLM inference proxy and connector management, plus maybe the MCP server for external agents.

This simplifies the plan: local orchestrator + local tools replicates the sidecar chat; sidecar offers LLM proxy and connector APIs. That's coherent.

But the user might expect the existing sidecar chat's "enhanced capabilities" (richer model with tool calling) when connected. With local orchestrator + sidecar LLM proxy, we still get tool calling from the model; the local orchestrator handles tools. So no loss. Good.

What about the existing `/api/chat` used by other clients? Keep it unchanged. The SPA switches to local orchestrator always, with model providers. The sidecar's `/api/chat` remains for compatibility/CLI? The CLI has interactive chat maybe uses its own. Fine.

### New sidecar endpoints

To support local orchestrator with sidecar:
- `POST /api/llm/chat` (streaming OpenAI-compatible completion proxy). Request: `{base_url, api_key, model, messages, tools?, tool_choice?}`. Response: SSE passthrough or normalized JSON. Security: don't log secrets; CORS restricted; local only. Could proxy raw OpenAI SSE. This is small.
  - Alternatively `/api/llm/chat/completions` passthrough to `${base_url}/chat/completions`. Keep path.
  - Health endpoint already exists.
- Maybe `GET /api/tools` and `POST /api/tools/{name}` for external MCP tools. But current chat only uses core MCP tools, which local handles. If we want to expose MCP-backed tools in the future, add later. For now, no need. But the enhanced capability "MCP" could be represented by the sidecar's ability to manage connectors; not chat. We can defer.
- `GET /api/capabilities` should return a structured manifest: backend, features, version. Currently returns `{"capabilities": backend}`. We can enrich without breaking? The SPA can use a new `GET /api/capabilities/manifest` or extend. Since only internal, extend to `{backend, features: {...}, version}`. Tests update. Worker can synthesize local manifest when sidecar absent. Or the SPA can detect via `GET /api/config` and use local capabilities. For graceful detection, a dedicated endpoint is cleaner.
- Maybe `POST /api/import` / `GET /api/export` for local-to-sidecar handoff. User chose local source of truth, so sidecar import is optional. But "enhanced capabilities" may want to push local data to sidecar for CLI/MCP access. We can offer one-way "Publish local work to sidecar" via existing CRUD endpoints (loop) or a new bulk endpoint. Since local is source of truth, sidecar becomes a read-only mirror for CLI/MCP. Need to avoid sidecar mutations. Could implement `POST /api/import` bulk with idempotent upsert, and a "Sync to sidecar" action. Maybe phase 2. Or skip for v1; the user didn't ask for it. But if chat uses sidecar's MCP for anything, it would be stale. Since local orchestrator handles data, sidecar data is only used by CLI/MCP agents. The "publish" feature is valuable but optional.

### Direct browser LLM and built-in AI

Providers:
- `OpenAICompatibleProvider`: direct `fetch` to `${base_url}/chat/completions`, streaming SSE. User config in Settings: base URL, API key, model. CORS caveat displayed in Settings; test button. We can also support no-key local endpoints.
- `BrowserBuiltInProvider`: feature detect:
  - Chrome: `window.LanguageModel` (new) or `window.ai.languageModel` (older). Use `create()` with `monitor` download progress. `promptStreaming()`.
  - Maybe `window.ai.assistant` (deprecated). We'll support a narrow adapter.
  - The built-in model may not support tools; use a "structured intent" approach: send a system prompt asking for JSON with optional `tool_calls`? Or keep it text-only and let users use slash commands/UI for mutations. The user wants chat; text-only is acceptable, but "conversation is the product" suggests mutations. We can implement a lightweight local intent layer: the browser model returns a JSON envelope `{reply, action?: {tool, arguments}}` using `responseConstraint` if supported; otherwise plain text. To keep scope manageable, we can implement tool calling only for OpenAI-compatible/sidecar providers; built-in model is text-only with a note in Settings ("advice only; actions need a tool-capable model or sidecar"). That's honest progressive disclosure.
  - Alternatively, use Chrome's built-in Prompt API with a JSON schema constraint to extract tool calls; doable. But experimental and version-dependent. Plan can include it as best-effort.

- `DeterministicProvider`: always available; port `offline_fallback` and slash command handling. It can also answer based on local canvas (e.g., list jobs/outcomes). It doesn't call tools unless the user uses slash commands / explicit actions. This is the guaranteed floor.

Model selection UX: Settings "Assistant" section:
- Mode: "On this device (no model)" / "Browser model (if available)" / "Custom model endpoint" / "Local sidecar".
- Auto-select best available, with manual override.
- Show capability status, privacy note, and "Test connection".
- Built-in model download UI (progress).
- Direct endpoint CORS warning.

<skill_content name="writing-plans">
# Skill: writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write implementation plans for an engineer who has not seen this codebase or this spec. Assume they write idiomatic code in the project's language once they know the exact interface and the exact test, and that they will make a reasonable choice wherever the plan leaves one open. What they cannot know is what you decided: which files, which names and signatures, which values from the spec, which tests prove each task. Document those. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Step Granularity

**Each step is one action with a checkable result:**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

## Review Focus

[The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
— one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
owns the code, in that task's own step style.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `function(input: InputType) -> ResultType` in `exact/path/to/file.py`**

One line on the approach when the signature and the test leave a choice
(which library call, which data structure); a code block only for an
algorithm they do not determine.

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## What a Step Contains

A step is done when the implementer can write exactly one reasonable thing
from it. That is the whole requirement: unambiguous, not complete. Each kind
of step carries what makes it unambiguous and nothing more:

- **A test step:** the test's name and its assertions, as code, with the
  spec's exact values in them.
- **A code step:** the exact signature (name, parameters, return type), the
  file it lives in, and the specific values the spec pins. The implementer
  writes the body. A body appears only for an algorithm the signature and
  tests do not determine, or for exact copy the spec fixes.
- **A verification step:** the command to run and the output that means it
  passed.
- **A reference to another task:** that task's Interfaces block says what
  to use; the plan does not repeat that task's code.

A plan is the set of decisions the implementer cannot make alone. A plan
longer than the code it describes has written the code instead. Lines that
decide nothing ("TBD", "handle edge cases", "add appropriate validation",
"write tests for the above", a type or function no task defines) are the
opposite failure, and the self-review catches both.

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

# Browser BFF: Run the Living Studio Without the Sidecar

## Goal

Make the hosted SPA fully usable in a browser with no sidecar, using a client-side BFF (`StudioBff`) and an IndexedDB-backed local store as the source of truth. When a sidecar is present, progressively expose its enhanced capabilities without silently moving or overwriting local data.

## Architecture

```text
UI (StudioContext, lenses, composer)
        │
        ▼
StudioBff façade ────────────── CapabilityRegistry
        │                              │
        ├── LocalDataService ──────────┐
        ├── LocalMemoryService ────────┤── IndexedDbStore (source of truth)
        ├── ChatOrchestrator           │
        │     ├── DeterministicProvider (always available)
        │     ├── BrowserModelProvider (if browser API exists)
        │     ├── DirectOpenAIProvider (if endpoint configured)
        │     └── SidecarLlmProvider (if sidecar connected)
        └── SidecarEnhancements (connectors, import, MCP)
                │
                ▼ same-origin /api/* only when capability is available
        Optional local sidecar (FastAPI)
```

The BFF is a client module in `apps/studio/src/bff/`, not a new server. The Cloudflare Worker remains static-assets-only; no Workers Containers required.

## Capability Matrix

| Capability | No sidecar | Sidecar present | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jobs, steps, outcomes, canvas, scoring | Yes, IndexedDB | Yes, IndexedDB | Local store is always authoritative |
| Deterministic ODI guidance | Yes | Yes | Port of the sidecar's offline fallback |
| Browser built-in model | If available | If available | Feature-detected; hidden when absent |
| Direct OpenAI-compatible endpoint | If reachable/CORS allows | Same | Sidecar proxy preferred when available |
| Sidecar LLM proxy | No | Yes | Avoids CORS and hides API keys |
| Connector registry / health | No | Yes | Filesystem-backed, sidecar-only |
| MCP/CLI shared data | No | Yes | Optional one-way import from sidecar |
| Local memory and conversation history | Yes | Yes | IndexedDB; optional sidecar import |
| Workspace import/export | Yes | Yes | JSON file, clear user action |

## Key Decisions

1. **Local data is authoritative.** Every canvas read and core mutation goes to IndexedDB, even when the sidecar is connected. The sidecar never silently owns core ODI data.
2. **IndexedDB behind a `LocalStore` seam.** Use `idb` plus `fake-indexeddb` for tests. The interface allows OPFS SQLite or native SQLite later without touching the domain layer. This avoids WASM/CSP/COOP complexity now.
3. **Chat runs locally, not through `/api/chat`.** The SPA gets a TS `ChatOrchestrator` that mirrors the existing tool loop and mutates the local store. This is required for local-first correctness. The sidecar `/api/chat` remains unchanged for other clients.
4. **Sidecar enhancement is explicit.** New `POST /api/llm/chat` proxies OpenAI-compatible model calls; existing connector endpoints stay sidecar-only. Capabilities are detected via a structured manifest.
5. **No automatic two-way sync in this slice.** Offer one-time import from sidecar when local is empty, plus JSON export/import. Automatic replication, E2EE, and multi-tenant sync remain future work.
6. **Hidden until available, with discrete discovery.** Enhanced UI is hidden when unavailable, but Settings always lists capability status and what connecting unlocks. One-time hints/toasts point to the upgrade path without nagging.

<skill_content name="executing-plans">
# Skill: executing-plans

# Executing Plans

Execute the plan yourself, task by task, in this session: no implementer
subagent per task, no reviewer per task. One fresh-context review of the
whole branch at the end.

**Why inline:** Subagent-driven development pays for a fresh implementer
and a fresh reviewer on every task, each re-reading the codebase from zero.
Inline execution pays for one context (yours) plus one reviewer at the end.
What it gives up is a fresh context per task and a second pair of eyes per
task. This skill keeps what those two things bought, by other means: the
brief is the spec, the ledger is your memory, TDD is the per-task gate, and
the final reviewer is the second pair of eyes.

**Core principle:** The plan already did the thinking. Execute it exactly,
prove each step with a test you watched fail and then pass, and leave a
record that survives your own forgetting.

**Narration:** between tool calls, narrate at most one short line — the
ledger and the tool results carry the record.

**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner
between tasks. They chose inline execution to spend less, not to answer
"should I continue?" after every task. Execute all tasks from the plan
without stopping.

**Rulings, not stalls.** Conflicts, ambiguities, plan defects — decide them.
The spec is the binding authority, the plan is its argument, and your
judgment settles what neither answers. Record every decision in the ledger
as `Ruling: <what you decided> — <why> — <what it costs if wrong>`, and keep
going. Deviating from the plan without a ledgered ruling is a decision made
in secret.

Four things stop you, and only these: an irreversible or destructive
operation; a security-sensitive action; a side effect outside this worktree
that norms say you ask about first (a merge, a push to a shared branch, a
publish); and a plan so broken that every path forward is a guess. For
those, stop and ask.

## When to Use

- You have a plan from superpowers:writing-plans and your human partner
  chose inline execution at the handoff.
- Your harness has no subagent tool (see the per-platform references in
  `../using-superpowers/references/`). Never fabricate a dispatch; run
  the plan here.
- Tasks are mostly independent — the same precondition as
  superpowers:subagent-driven-development.

A fully specified plan makes inline execution transcription plus testing:
it runs well on a mid-tier session model, and the one place the most
capable model earns its cost is the final review, which this skill
dispatches separately. Tell your human partner so when they choose inline.

Prefer superpowers:subagent-driven-development when your human partner
wants a review gate on every task, or when the plan is long enough that
its later tasks would run on a compacted context. Inline execution over a
long plan still works — the ledger is what makes it recoverable — but the
last tasks get the least of you.

## The Process

```dot

    rankdir=TB;

        "task-start: brief + BASE; read the brief" [shape=box];

        "Plan wrong? Rule and ledger. Code wrong? systematic-debugging" [shape=box];
        "Commit as the plan's commit steps say" [shape=box];
        "Completion contract met?" [shape=diamond];
        "task-done: run tests, ledger the result; mark todo complete" [shape=box];
    }

    "More tasks remain?" [shape=diamond];
    "Final whole-branch review (fresh reviewer if you have one)" [shape=box];

    "Final review clean: delete this plan's workspace" [shape=box];
    "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch" [shape=box style=filled fillcolor=lightgreen];

    "Setup: worktree, workspace + ledger, read plan + spec, pre-flight scan" -> "task-start: brief + BASE; read the brief";
    "task-start: brief + BASE; read the brief" -> "Work the steps in order: TDD, run every verification, read every output";
    "Work the steps in order: TDD, run every verification, read every output" -> "Step output matches plan's Expected?";
    "Step output matches plan's Expected?" -> "Plan wrong? Rule and ledger. Code wrong? systematic-debugging" [label="no"];
    "Plan wrong? Rule and ledger. Code wrong? systematic-debugging" -> "Work the steps in order: TDD, run every verification, read every output";
    "Step output matches plan's Expected?" -> "Commit as the plan's commit steps say" [label="yes, last step"];
    "Commit as the plan's commit steps say" -> "Completion contract met?";
    "Completion contract met?" -> "Work the steps in order: TDD, run every verification, read every output" [label="no - finish the task"];
    "Completion contract met?" -> "task-done: run tests, ledger the result; mark todo complete" [label="yes"];
    "task-done: run tests, ledger the result; mark todo complete" -> "More tasks remain?";
    "More tasks remain?" -> "task-start: brief + BASE; read the brief" [label="yes"];
    "More tasks remain?" -> "Final whole-branch review (fresh reviewer if you have one)" [label="no"];
    "Final whole-branch review (fresh reviewer if you have one)" -> "Re-grade, then: Critical/Important → ONE fix pass, each fix RED→GREEN + green suite; Minor → ledger";
    "Re-grade, then: Critical/Important → ONE fix pass, each fix RED→GREEN + green suite; Minor → ledger" -> "Final review clean: delete this plan's workspace";
    "Final review clean: delete this plan's workspace" -> "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch";
}
```

## Setup

Ensure the work happens in an isolated workspace: use
superpowers:using-git-worktrees to create one or verify the existing one.
Never start implementation on a main/master branch without your human
partner's explicit consent.

Conversation memory does not survive compaction. An inline executor that
loses its place re-implements tasks whose commits already exist — the same
failure as a controller re-dispatching them, paid for in your own context.
Track progress in a ledger file, not only in todos. Harness todos are a
live view; the ledger is the record.

The workspace and ledger are shared with superpowers:subagent-driven-development
— same directory, same format — so a plan can change executors mid-flight
and the new one resumes from the same ledger.

- Each plan owns a workspace: at skill start, run
  `../subagent-driven-development/scripts/sdd-workspace PLAN_FILE` — it
  prints the plan's git-ignored directory
  (`<repo-root>/.superpowers/sdd/<plan-basename>/`), home to every
  artifact for THIS plan: ledger, briefs, review packages. Another plan's
  directory is never yours to read or write.
- Check for this plan's ledger at `<workspace>/progress.md`. If its first
  line names your plan file, tasks with a `Task <N>: complete` line are
  DONE — do not redo them; resume at the first task without one. Their
  commits exist in git even when your context no longer remembers making
  them: after compaction, trust the ledger and `git log` over your own
  recollection. A ledger whose first line names a different plan file is
  another plan's progress: leave it and start your own, fresh.
- Create the ledger with its identity as the first line:
  `# SDD ledger — plan: <plan file path>`.
- `git clean -fdx` will destroy the workspace (it's git-ignored scratch);
  if that happens, recover from `git log`.

Read the plan once, note its context and Global Constraints, and create a
todo per task. If the plan names a Spec, read that too: the spec is the
authority the plan argues from, and conflicts inside the plan resolve
against it. A plan with no reachable spec gets a ledger note saying so —
rulings made without one are provisional.

**REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** load superpowers:test-driven-development now,
before Task 1. It governs every step of every task below; a plan whose
steps already say "write the failing test first" does not exempt you
from reading it.

Before Task 1, scan the plan for conflicts between tasks. The plan's
Interfaces blocks tell you where to look: for every task that consumes
what an earlier task produces, one ledger row — the two tasks, what one
produces against what the other consumes, and what you found. Tasks that
share nothing get no row; a plan whose tasks share nothing gets the single
line `Pre-flight: no shared interfaces`. Rule on each conflict a row
surfaces with the spec as the binding authority, record the ruling beside
its row, and start Task 1. Each task's own text is checked when you read
its brief, not here.

## The Task Loop

Everything you print, and every tool result, stays resident in your
context for the rest of the session. Redirect long test output to a file
in the workspace and read its tail; read a brief, not the whole plan.

### 1. Take the task

- Run this skill's `scripts/task-start PLAN_FILE N`. It prints the brief
  path and BASE (the commit the task's range is cut from) in one call.
  Read the brief for every task, including ones you remember from setup:
  what you remember is a summary, the brief has the exact values,
  signatures, and test cases.
- Mark the task's todo in_progress.

Every tool call is a turn that re-reads your whole context. Bookkeeping
rides along with work — a ledger append in the same call as the commit,
never in a call of its own.

### 2. Work the steps

The plan's steps are already in RED-GREEN order; follow them in that
order under superpowers:test-driven-development, loaded at setup. A test
step's code is written first and run first. Watching it fail is a step,
not a formality — a test that passes before the implementation exists is
a finding about the test.

Every step that runs a command has an `Expected:` line. Run the command,
read its output, and compare. Three outcomes:

- **Matches.** Next step.
- **The code is wrong.** Use superpowers:systematic-debugging. Find the
  cause; never patch the symptom to make the step's output match.
- **The plan is wrong** — a step contradicts the spec, an interface from an
  earlier task doesn't match what this task consumes, a command that
  cannot work. Rule on the smallest change that satisfies the spec, ledger
  it as `Task <N>: Ruling: <finding> — <what you decided and why>`, and
  continue. The ruling is carried, not remembered: later tasks that touch
  the same interface read it from the ledger.

Commit as the plan's commit steps say. A task that spans several commits
is fine; BASE is what the review range is cut from, never `HEAD~1`.

### 3. The completion contract

Before a task's ledger line, all of the following are true, with evidence
in this session — not inferred from the diff looking right:

- Every test the brief names exists and ran in this task, and you read
  the output.
- The final test run for the task passed — `task-done` is that run, and
  it writes the command and result into the ledger line.
- Every `Expected:` line in the brief was compared against real output.
- Every deviation from the brief has a `Ruling:` line in the ledger.

**REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** superpowers:verification-before-completion governs
the claim. If any item is missing, the task is not complete: finish it.

### 4. Complete the task

Run this skill's `scripts/task-done PLAN_FILE N BASE -- <test command>`
with the test command the brief names for the whole task. It runs the
tests, keeps the full output in the workspace, prints the tail, and — only
if they pass — appends the completion line to the ledger:

`Task <N>: complete (commits <base7>..<head7>, tests: <command> → <result>)`

A failing run records nothing; the task is not complete. When it records,
mark the todo complete and take the next task.

## Final Review

Run `../subagent-driven-development/scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE MERGE_BASE HEAD`
(MERGE_BASE = the commit the branch started from, e.g.
`git merge-base main HEAD`) and review from the file it prints.

**With a subagent tool:** dispatch the reviewer on the most capable
available model — the whole-branch review is a judgment task — using
superpowers:requesting-code-review's
[code-reviewer.md](../requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md), with the
package path, the plan and spec paths, the plan's Review Focus section
verbatim if it has one (the input classes and failure modes the plan's
tests do not exercise — the reviewer checks each deliberately), and a
pointer to the ledger's `Ruling:` lines so it can weigh the calls you
made. Specify the model
explicitly; an omitted model inherits the session's, which may not be the
most capable. This is the one fresh context the whole run buys. Do not
skip it, and do not replace it with your own read of the diff.

**Without a subagent tool:** read code-reviewer.md and perform that review
yourself against the package, as a separate pass after the last task's
ledger line. Write `Final review: self-review (no subagent tool)` to the
ledger, and say so in your final message: a self-review by the author is
weaker than a fresh reviewer, and your human partner decides whether that
is enough before merge.

Sort the findings before you act on any of them. The reviewer's severity
labels are advice; the gate is yours. Its "Declined to judge" list is
yours too: every line there is a ruling you make and ledger, exactly like
a plan conflict — `Final: Ruling: <behavior the reviewer set aside> —
<what a reasonable person using this software gets, and why that stands
or why it is now a finding> — <cost if wrong>`. Re-grade first, by effect: the
spec is a vision document, and a finding's grade is what a reasonable
person using this software gets if it ships, not whether the spec names
the input that triggers it — a reviewer who set a finding at Minor
because the spec was silent has graded the spec, not the effect. Then:

- **Critical and Important** enter the fix pass.
- **Minor** goes to the ledger as `Final: minor (deferred): <one-liner>`
  and to your final message under "Deferred minors". Minors never enter
  the fix pass, and never become rulings — a ruling is a decision about a
  conflict, not a note that you declined a polish suggestion.

Fix the Critical and Important findings yourself — you are the
implementer here — in ONE pass. Each fix is verified by TDD, not by a
second reviewer: write the test that reproduces the finding, watch it
fail, make it pass, then run the whole suite. Record each in the ledger as
`Final: fixed <finding> — <test name> RED→GREEN, suite <N>/<N>`. A fix
without a test that failed first is not verified; a suite that is not
green after the pass means the pass is not over. Do not dispatch a
re-review: it would re-read a diff whose covering tests already answer
"addressed" and whose suite run already answers "broke nothing".

A finding you decide not to fix is a ruling — `Final: Ruling: <finding> —
<why the code stands> — <cost if wrong>` — and reaches your human partner
in the rulings list. There is no second fix pass.

## Finish

Before you delete anything, collect every ledger line containing
`Ruling:` into your final message under "Rulings I made", in the order you
made them, each with what it costs if wrong, and every `minor (deferred)`
line under "Deferred minors". Both lists are exhaustive. Your final
message is the only place the decisions you took on your human partner's
behalf — and the findings you chose not to act on — reach them.

When the final review is clean and its fixes are committed, delete this
plan's workspace directory — the git history is the record now. Sibling
directories belong to other plans; leave them alone.

Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "I remember what Task N says" | You remember a summary. The brief has the exact values. Read it. |
| "The plan's code is right, skip watching the test fail" | A test you never saw fail proves nothing. It is one step. Run it. |
| "I'll run the full suite at the end instead of per step" | Per-step runs are how you learn which step broke it. The end-of-task run is the contract, not a substitute. |
| "The plan is wrong here, I'll just do the right thing" | Do the right thing and ledger the ruling. Unledgered deviation is a decision made in secret. |
| "I'll write the ledger lines after a few tasks" | Compaction does not wait for a convenient moment. One line per task, in the same message as the commit. |
| "Let me check in before the next task" | They chose inline to spend less. Progress prompts spend their time instead. Only the four stops stop you. |
| "I read my own diff carefully; the final reviewer is redundant" | Same author, same blind spots. The reviewer is the only fresh context this run buys. |
| "Tests should pass, the change was trivial" | "Should" is not evidence. The contract requires the command and its output. |
| "Subagents are slow and expensive, I'll skip the final review too" | Inline already removed the per-task reviewers. One review of the whole branch is the floor, not the ceiling. |
| "The reviewer said Minor, so it's Minor" | The label graded the spec's silence. Grade what the person gets. Re-grade, then gate. |
| "The fix is obvious, no need for a failing test first" | The failing test is the only proof the finding was real and is now gone. Without it you have a diff and a hope. |
| "I'll fix the minors too while I'm in there" | Every minor you fix is a test, a fix, and a suite run your partner did not ask for. Ledger them; your partner decides. |

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  # A PR with no description gives a reviewer nothing to check the diff
  # against, so an empty body fails the build before any expensive job runs.
  pr-body:
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - name: Require a non-empty pull request body
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          body="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" --json body --jq '.body')"
          if [ -z "$(printf '%s' "$body" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
            echo "::error::The pull request body is empty. Summarize the change and how you verified it."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: pull request body is present"

  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Ruff Lint (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Verify Ruff Formatting (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

      - name: Verify the mascot assets match the generator
        run: uv run python brand/tools/render.py --check

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Mypy
        run: uv run mypy apps brand packages

      - name: Run Mypy (website)
        run: uv run --directory website mypy .

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Bandit
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages

      - name: Run Bandit (website)
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r website/

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Pytest
        run: |
          uv run pytest \
            --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
            --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
            --cov=agentic_odi_core \
            --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
            --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
            --cov-report=term-missing \
            --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml

      - name: Upload coverage report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: coverage.xml
          if-no-files-found: error

      # One upload per run is enough; the 3.12 report is the canonical one.
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ matrix.python-version == '3.12' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v7
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: CLI reports a version
        run: |
          version="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli --version)"
          [ -n "$version" ]
          echo "OK: $version"

      - name: CLI exposes connectors commands
        run: |
          help="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors --help)"
          echo "$help" | grep -q list
          echo "$help" | grep -q ingest
          echo "OK: connectors help"

      - name: Installer installs from a simulated release
        run: bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh

      - name: MCP server boots and serves /mcp
        run: |
          uv run python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server > /tmp/mcp_server.log 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sfX POST http://localhost:8000/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
              -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "MCP server did not respond on :8000/mcp"
            cat /tmp/mcp_server.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: MCP server responded with 200"

      - name: Living Studio sidecar serves the studio API
        run: |
          AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND=mcp uv run python -m agentic_odi_studio_api.main > /tmp/sidecar.log 2>&1 &
          SIDECAR_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/health/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}' -o /dev/null &&
              curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/canvas?mcp_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp" -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "Living Studio sidecar did not respond on :8100"
            cat /tmp/sidecar.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: sidecar studio API responded with 200"

      - name: scripts/dev.py brings up both services and stops cleanly
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/dev.py > /tmp/clientrun.log 2>&1 &
          RUN_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/config &&
              curl -sfX POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp \
                -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
                -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "scripts/dev.py did not bring up both services"
            cat /tmp/clientrun.log
            kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi

              -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \

          probe() {

              -d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}' -o /dev/null &&

          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "Living Studio sidecar did not respond on :8100"
            cat /tmp/sidecar.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: sidecar studio API responded with 200"

      - name: scripts/dev.py brings up both services and stops cleanly
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/dev.py > /tmp/clientrun.log 2>&1 &
          RUN_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/config &&
              curl -sfX POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp \
                -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
                -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "scripts/dev.py did not bring up both services"
            cat /tmp/clientrun.log
            kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi

# Development

Everything below mirrors what CI runs. Install the workspace first:

```bash
uv sync --all-packages
```

## Linting, Formatting & Type Checks

Shared tooling lives in the root `pyproject.toml`, so one command covers every
Python project:

```bash
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run mypy apps brand packages
uv run --directory website mypy .

# Security scanning
uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages website/
```

## Frontend & Desktop Checks (studio)

The SPA and Tauri shell mirror their CI jobs locally:

```bash
npm --prefix apps/studio run lint       # ESLint
npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck  # tsc --noEmit
npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run  # Vitest (run once)
npm --prefix apps/studio run build      # production build → apps/studio/dist
cd apps/studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check
```

### Conversational UI coverage

The agent-composed surfaces and the first-run tour are covered at these levels:

| File | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `apps/studio/src/ui/protocol.test.ts` | Spec parsing: prop types, enums, ranges, required props, depth/node/size ceilings, unknown types |
| `apps/studio/src/ui/UiRenderer.test.tsx` | Card rendering, computed opportunity scores, action dispatch, per-node failure isolation, catalog/registry parity |
| `apps/studio/src/components/chat/Conversation.test.tsx` | Prose and surfaces interleaved in the agent's order; card actions become messages |
| `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_ui_spec.py` | Catalog validation and `render_ui` tool-schema generation |
| `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_chat_ui.py` | `render_ui` interception, `ui` SSE events, and the correction fed back to the model |
| `apps/studio/src/features/flags.test.ts` | Flag precedence (query → storage → env → default), value parsing, local overrides |
| `apps/studio/src/onboarding/machine.test.ts` | Tour transitions, no forward motion without a goal, versioned storage, malformed records |
| `apps/studio/src/onboarding/FirstRunWizard.test.tsx` | Auto-open, full flow to a destination, skip/Escape, focus trap, resume, replay, inline model repair, flag off |
| `apps/studio/src/App.test.tsx` | First-run ordering: tour over the context conversation, job handoff, chosen surface opens, flag off in shell tests |

## Website Checks (GitHub Pages)

The `website/` static site is part of the main CI workflow. Its tests assert the
committed OG art is reproducible, that `index.html` stays in sync with the
README, and that the publish pipeline (`website/tests/test_pages_deploy.py`)
still exists:

```bash
uv run --directory website pytest tests/
```

Publishing happens in `.github/workflows/pages.yml`: it runs those tests, builds
`_site` from `website/`, and deploys the artifact with `actions/deploy-pages` on
every push to `main`. There is no `gh-pages` branch, so that workflow is the only
thing that keeps <https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/> online.

## Formatting workflow

- **When editing Python files**, either rely on the **pre-commit hooks** below
  (recommended) or run Ruff formatting directly before pushing:

  ```bash
  uv run ruff format .
  ```

- **CI behavior**:
  - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files.
  - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only.
  - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the
    changes, and push again.

## Pre-commit hooks

To run the checks automatically before each commit:

```bash
uv tool install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` run on staged files whenever you commit.
You can also trigger them manually:

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
```

## Testing

Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely
in-memory — no running server required. Tests live next to the package they
cover, and every test runs from the repository root:

```bash
uv run pytest                        # everything
uv run pytest apps/cli               # one app
uv run pytest packages/core          # one package
uv run pytest tests/contract         # cross-package contracts
uv run pytest tests/scripts          # dev launcher
```

The MCP server contract test compares the live FastMCP registry with
`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py`, so add or change a tool in
both places. The CLI local-backend contract test keeps `_LOCAL_HANDLERS` aligned
with the same tool names.

## Test Coverage

CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and uploads one combined
`coverage.xml` from the 3.12 job to
[Codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi).

The Codecov upload authenticates with the `CODECOV_TOKEN` repository secret and
is non-blocking (`fail_ci_if_error: false`), so a Codecov outage or a fork PR
without secrets cannot fail the test job. The badge at the top of the README
tracks `main`, which is the baseline every PR is compared against:

- **Project** status requires at least **90%** coverage (`target: 90%`) and
  tolerates a 1% dip from `codecov.yml`.
- **Patch** status is informational for now, so new code can land while the
  suite catches up.

To reproduce the report locally:

```bash
uv run pytest \
  --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
  --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
  --cov=agentic_odi_core \
  --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
  --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
  --cov-report=term-missing \
  --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml
```

> [!NOTE]
> Coverage is only collected for the Python packages. `apps/studio/` and test
> directories are excluded in `codecov.yml`.

### Conventions

- Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named
  `test_*.py`.
- Root `tests/` is reserved for cross-package checks (`contract/` and
  `scripts/`).
- Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`.
- Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests.
- The MCP server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before
  each test.

### Test Coverage Map

| Area | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `packages/core/tests/` | Domain models, opportunity scoring, `ODIService`, repository implementations, SQLite persistence, schema, and repository factory |
| `apps/mcp-server/tests/` | Full ODI workflow, entity parity, context tools, Customer Outcomes, evidence, tool errors, and HTTP transport startup |
| `apps/studio-api/tests/` | Health, config, canvas, SSE chat, SPA fallback, MCP hydration, probes, and step/outcome passthrough |
| `apps/cli/tests/` | Backend selection, local/remote CRUD, chat, wizard, onboarding, updates, rendering, connectors, and startup performance |
| `packages/connectors/tests/` | Catalog presets, registry persistence, factory, MCP and REST connectors, evidence mapping, and sink |
| `tests/contract/` | Live MCP tool surface and CLI local-handler parity |
| `tests/scripts/` | `scripts/dev.py` startup, port checks, signals, and shutdown |
| `apps/studio/src/**/*.test.ts` | SPA units: ODI math, transport bridge, SSE parser, sidecar client |
| `website/tests/` | Static site integrity, OG art reproducibility, and README sync |

> [!TIP]
> Type `/test` in the AI assistant to have the agent run all tests and report the
> results automatically.

package = false

members = [
    "apps/cli",

    "apps/studio-api",
    "packages/connectors",
    "packages/core",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "bandit==1.9.4",
    "jinja2==3.1.6",

    "mypy==2.4.0",
    "pyinstaller==6.22.3",
    "pygments==2.21.0",
    "pytest==9.1.1",
    "pytest-asyncio==1.4.0",
    "pytest-cov==7.1.0",
    "ruff==0.17.1",
    "pillow==12.3.0",
]

[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = [".venv", "tests", ".worktrees", "node_modules"]

[tool.ruff]

extend-exclude = [".agents/skills", ".worktrees", "docs/superpowers/plans"]

]

  tauri-build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm ci
        working-directory: apps/studio

      # Dependabot PRs cannot read repository secrets, so the signing key is
      # empty there. Export it only when present and disable updater artifacts
      # otherwise; passing an empty key makes the bundler try (and fail) to
      # decode it.
      - name: Build desktop bundle
        working-directory: apps/studio
        env:
          SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$SIGNING_KEY"
            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="$SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD"
            npm run tauri -- build
          else
            echo "No TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY provided — building without signed updater artifacts."
            npm run tauri -- build --config '{"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}'
          fi

      - name: Upload desktop bundles
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: tauri-bundles-linux
          if-no-files-found: warn
          path: |
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/*.deb
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage.sig

  ci-green:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test, smoke, website, studio, tauri-check, tauri-build]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Verify all required jobs succeeded
        run: |
          results='${{ join(needs.*.result, ' ') }}'
          echo "Job results: $results"
          for result in $results; do
            if [ "$result" != "success" ]; then
              echo "::error::A required job did not succeed ($results)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "OK: all required jobs succeeded"

# Browser BFF for Living Studio

Date: 2026-10-24
Status: Approved

## Problem

The hosted Living Studio depends on a Python sidecar for canvas CRUD, chat, memory,
connectors, and model access. Cloudflare Pages serves the SPA only; without a
reachable sidecar the studio is unusable. We want the hosted studio to be useful
on its own while preserving the richer local experience when a sidecar is running.

## Decision

Add a client-side backend-for-frontend (BFF) inside the SPA. The BFF owns local
data, local memory, capability discovery, and chat orchestration. IndexedDB is the
source of truth for ODI data. The sidecar becomes an optional enhancement provider
for connectors, MCP, CLI integration, and server-side model proxying.

No new hosted server is introduced.

## Architecture

```
React components
  -> StudioContext
    -> StudioBff facade
      -> CapabilityRegistry
      -> LocalDataService  -> LocalStore (IndexedDB, in-memory fallback)
      -> LocalMemoryService ->
      -> ChatOrchestrator -> deterministic local assistant
                           -> browser built-in model (feature detected)
                           -> OpenAI-compatible endpoint (direct fetch)
                           -> sidecar /api/llm/chat (when available)
      -> SidecarEnhancements -> existing /api/* endpoints
```

### Local data

IndexedDB database `agentic-odi-studio` version 1 with stores `meta`, `jobs`,
`steps`, `outcomes`, `observations`, `conversations`, and `turns`. A `LocalStore`
interface isolates persistence so tests use `fake-indexeddb` and browsers without
IndexedDB fall back to an in-memory store for the session.

Domain behavior mirrors `packages/core`: job/step/outcome CRUD, insertion order,
opportunity score `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`, step cascade
on job delete, outcome cascade on step delete, and input validation.

### Capabilities

`CapabilityRegistry` probes and exposes:

| Capability | Availability |
| --- | --- |
| `local-data` | always |
| `local-memory` | always |
| `deterministic-assistant` | always |
| `browser-model` | feature detected |
| `endpoint-model` | configured endpoint URL + model |
| `sidecar-llm` | sidecar capability probe |
| `sidecar-connectors` | sidecar capability probe |
| `sidecar-mcp` | sidecar capability probe |
| `sidecar-import` | sidecar capability probe |

Enhanced controls are hidden when unavailable. Settings shows a compact status
list and the chat empty state links to it. Toasts/hints explain that running the
local sidecar unlocks connectors and MCP.

### Assistant and memory

`ChatOrchestrator` streams events in the existing SSE shape (`message`, `chunk`,
`tool`, `tool_result`, `ui`, `done`, `error`) so the current conversation UI keeps
working. The deterministic assistant answers common questions about the canvas
and supports core jobs/steps/outcomes plus `remember` and `render_ui`. External
models use the OpenAI-compatible tool loop. Sidecar chat remains available as an
enhancement and for tools that only exist server-side.

Conversation history and observations are stored locally. A one-time import from
the sidecar fills the local store only when it is empty. JSON workspace export and
import are provided; automatic replication and E2EE are deliberately deferred.

### Sidecar

The existing `/api/chat` endpoint is unchanged for other clients. Add:

- `POST /api/llm/chat`: streaming OpenAI-compatible proxy that keeps provider keys
  server-side and avoids browser CORS restrictions.
- `GET /api/capabilities`: capability manifest used by the SPA probe.
- Existing CRUD/memory endpoints remain for import and enhancement use.

### Hosted worker

`infra/cloudflare/worker.ts` returns a local-only capability manifest with status
200 when `SIDECAR_URL` is absent. CSP `connect-src` is built from `LLM_ORIGINS`
(defaults limited to localhost plus curated providers) so direct browser model
calls are allowed only where configured.

## Risks

- IndexedDB is origin-scoped. Hosted and desktop origins do not share data; export
  is available for moving a workspace.
- Browser built-in LLM APIs are not universally available. Detection must be
  conservative and the UI must hide the option when absent.
- Direct provider calls expose the user's key to the browser by design; the
  sidecar proxy is the recommended path when available.
- No automatic sync means local and sidecar data can diverge. The one-time import
  and explicit export/import make the boundary visible.

## Acceptance

- The hosted SPA can create and edit canvas data with no sidecar.
- Local data survives reload in an IndexedDB-capable browser.
- The deterministic assistant can read and mutate the canvas.
- Enhanced features stay hidden unless detected; Settings reports why.
- Existing sidecar behavior and Python tests remain green.
- `npm --prefix apps/studio run lint|typecheck|test|build` and `uv run pytest` pass.

# Browser BFF implementation plan

Date: 2026-10-24
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-24-browser-bff-design.md`

## Task 1: Local persistence and domain parity

- Add `idb` and `fake-indexeddb`.
- Create `apps/studio/src/bff/store/` with a `LocalStore` interface, IndexedDB
  implementation, and in-memory fallback.
- Create `apps/studio/src/bff/data/localDataService.ts` mirroring the Python ODI
  service: canvas read model, job/step/outcome CRUD, scoring, validation, and
  cascading deletes.
- Tests: store durability with `fake-indexeddb`, score math, insertion order,
  cascade behavior, and validation.

## Task 2: Capabilities and UI integration

- Create `CapabilityRegistry` with local, browser-model, endpoint-model, and
  sidecar probes.
- Add `StudioBff` facade.
- Route `StudioContext` canvas CRUD through `StudioBff` instead of the sidecar.
- Add capability status to Settings, hide enhanced controls when unavailable, and
  update the offline notice.
- Add a `localAssistant` feature flag.
- Tests: registry detection and Settings rendering.

## Task 3: Local assistant and memory

- Create `LocalMemoryService` for observations, conversations, turns, and prompt
  context.
- Create `ChatOrchestrator`: deterministic assistant, browser model, endpoint
  model, and sidecar proxy selection.
- Implement local core tools (`get_canvas`, job/step/outcome CRUD,
  `compute_opportunity`, `evaluate_outcome`, `remember`, `render_ui`).
- Stream the existing SSE event shape.
- Tests: deterministic tool calls, memory writes, event ordering, model selection.

## Task 4: Sidecar continuity and enhancements

- Add `GET /api/capabilities` and `POST /api/llm/chat` to the sidecar.
- Add one-time import from sidecar when local storage is empty.
- Add workspace JSON export/import.
- Keep existing `/api/chat` unchanged.
- Tests: capability manifest, proxy request shape, import/export round trip.

## Task 5: Hosted hardening

- Worker returns a local-only capability manifest when `SIDECAR_URL` is absent.
- Build CSP `connect-src` from `LLM_ORIGINS`.
- Update `wrangler.jsonc` documentation.
- Tests: worker response and CSP construction.

## Task 6: Documentation and verification

- Update `README.md`, `docs/living-studio.md`, `docs/deployment.md`, and
  `docs/architecture/*`.
- Regenerate `apps/studio/openapi.json` and `src/api/schema.d.ts`.
- Run lint, typecheck, unit tests, build, and `uv run pytest`.
- Push branch and open a PR with a non-empty body; wait for CI.

Existing App.test mocks studioApi. If we move imports to bff, tests break. We can modify `studioApi.fetchCanvas` etc. to route through BFF while retaining exported API. However `streamChat` also. And test mocks override studioApi entirely, so StudioContext remains testable. That's elegant: implement BFF and have studioApi delegate to it. But studioApi is the sidecar client; we can add BFF as the primary for data/chat and fall back to sidecar enhancements. Yet functions like `fetchCanvas` signature includes mcpUrl. We can ignore mcpUrl for local. For chat, `streamChat` delegates to BFF. That minimizes StudioContext changes; capability state still needs exposure to UI. We can add a separate `useCapabilities` hook or context.

But user wanted StudioContext switch to BFF. Indirection via studioApi still effectively switches; but cleaner to modify StudioContext imports directly and update tests? That's riskier. Alternative: create `studioApi` delegation and keep names; then all UI automatically uses local. Sidecar features (connectors, memory, conversation) could remain sidecar or local. But if `fetchMemory` routes local, memory panel works. `fetchLatestConversation` local. `createConversation` local. That's good.

However StudioContext's boot still calls `fetchConfig()` from sidecar to set defaults and `sidecarReachable`. We can make `fetchConfig` fall back to local defaults on failure. Then hosted works. `checkConnections` calls healthMcp/healthLlm which fail and show offline; we'll update OfflineNotice to say assistant local. Better: capabilities hook.

Let's implement BFF and have studioApi delegate:
- `fetchCanvas` -> `getBff().data.fetchCanvas()`
- `createJob`, etc. -> bff.
- `streamChat` -> bff.chat.stream
- memory funcs -> bff.memory
- conversations -> bff.memory
- connectors stay sidecar (enhancement)
- `fetchConfig` fallback local defaults.
- `healthLlm` could check capability and return local health. But UI currently sets offlineReply based on event; local assistant emits status offline? We can modify OfflineNotice to use capabilities, but it only uses llmHealth. We can make `healthLlm` return `{healthy:true,message:"Local assistant ready"}` when local assistant available? That would hide the notice. Better add capability context and update OfflineNotice. But simplest: return healthy true for local assistant, and update Settings "Model" status to "local assistant". We can expose capabilities via a module hook.

Maybe create `useCapabilities` hook that polls registry, but more work. We can add capabilities to StudioContext value. That requires modifying context interface and provider. Let's do it. Tests mocking studioApi will still get capabilities from registry; okay, but registry might probe sidecar and produce async state. Could cause act warnings. Hmm.

Given CI green priority, minimize changes to existing tests. Adding new context field is fine; tests use full provider and may not care. But async capability probing may cause test warnings. Use lazy capability detection with immediate local values and sidecar probe later.

Let's define types.

`StoredJob = Job & { seq: number; created_at: string; updated_at: string }`
`StoredStep = Step & { id: string; job_id: string; name: string; order: number; created_at: string; updated_at: string }`
`StoredOutcome = Outcome & { id: string; job_id: string; statement: string; importance: number|null; satisfaction: number|null; opportunity_score: number|null; created_at: string; updated_at: string }`

Store interface:
```ts
export interface LocalStore {
  readonly durable: boolean;
  init(): Promise<void>;
  close(): void;
  nextSeq(): Promise<number>;
  listJobs(): Promise<StoredJob[]>;
  getJob(id: string): Promise<StoredJob | undefined>;
  putJob(job: StoredJob): Promise<void>;
  deleteJob(id: string): Promise<void>;
  listSteps(jobId?: string): Promise<StoredStep[]>;
  getStep(id: string): Promise<StoredStep | undefined>;
  putStep(step: StoredStep): Promise<void>;
  deleteStep(id: string): Promise<void>;
  listOutcomes(jobId?: string): Promise<StoredOutcome[]>;
  getOutcome(id: string): Promise<StoredOutcome | undefined>;
  putOutcome(outcome: StoredOutcome): Promise<void>;
  deleteOutcome(id: string): Promise<void>;
  listObservations(): Promise<Observation[]>;
  putObservation(o: Observation): Promise<void>;
  deleteObservation(id: string): Promise<void>;
  clearObservations(): Promise<void>;
  listConversations(): Promise<Conversation[]>;
  getConversation(id): Promise<Conversation | undefined>;
  putConversation(c): Promise<void>;
  listTurns(conversationId): Promise<ConversationTurn[]>;
  appendTurn(t: Omit<ConversationTurn,'id'>): Promise<ConversationTurn>;
  clearTurns(conversationId): Promise<void>;
  clearAll(): Promise<void>;
}
```
For in-memory, `appendTurn` increments global turn id. For IDB, autoIncrement.

Deleting cascade can be in data service using store methods, but not atomic. Fine for v1. Better store method `deleteJobCascade` and `deleteStepCascade`. But memory store too. Implement in data service with list/delete; okay.

`nextSeq` in store meta. For memory store, counter.

IndexedDB schema indexes. Need `idb` types. We'll write.

`openLocalStore()`:
```ts
export async function openLocalStore(): Promise<LocalStore> {
  if (typeof indexedDB === "undefined") return new MemoryLocalStore();
  try { const store = new IndexedDbLocalStore(); await store.init(); return store; } catch { return new MemoryLocalStore(); }
}
```

Data service:
- `fetchCanvas()` reads all jobs sorted seq, steps sorted by order then seq, outcomes sorted seq. Return source local.
- `createJob`: validate; `nextSeq`; put; return strip.
- `updateJob`: if not found throw not_found; merge; trim.
- `addStep`: job exists; order integer; name; nextSeq.
- `updateStep`: validate order/name; if job? no.
- `addOutcome`: job exists; step if given exists and belongs to job; values 1..10; score.
- `updateOutcome`: validate; if step_id? UI payload doesn't include; okay.
- `deleteJob`: list steps, delete their outcomes, delete steps, delete job.
- `deleteStep`: delete outcomes for step.
- `computeOpportunity(importance, satisfaction)`.
- `evaluateOutcome` maybe deterministic guidance.

Errors:
```ts
export class BffError extends Error {
  readonly studioError: StudioError;
  constructor(code, message, opts) ...
}
export function bffError(...)
```
Update `asStudioError` to check `studioError`.

Memory service:
- matches Python behavior. `addObservation(kind,text,data,confidence,confirmed)`, status confirmed if confirmed.
- `listObservations(includeDismissed=false)`.
- `updateObservation`.
- `createConversation`, `latestConversation`, `listTurns`, `appendTurn`, `clear`.
- `memoryContext(maxChars)`.

Chat orchestrator:
This is the hardest. Need local assistant with tools.

We can simplify but functional:
- `stream(request, onEvent, signal)`:
  - Resolve conversation: if request.conversation_id exists and store has it, else create new and emit `conversation`.
  - Persist user turn.
  - Determine provider:
    - If `browser` available and no endpoint/sidecar? We'll implement endpoint and sidecar. Browser built-in detection maybe `window.ai`/`LanguageModel`; implement but tests can mock.
    - Sidecar if capabilities.sidecarLlm.
    - Endpoint if settings base_url and model_name not default local? The default config points to localhost:8001 which may be down; if endpoint fetch fails, fall back deterministic.
  - Always try remote then fallback deterministic? The user's goal: hosted works. If no remote, deterministic.
  - Emit `status` phases.
  - For deterministic: parse user message intent; execute tool(s); emit `tool`/`tool_result`/`canvas_dirty`/`memory`/`delta`/`message`; append assistant turn.
  - For endpoint: OpenAI chat completions with tools. Tool loop max 4. Stream deltas if possible; tool calls collect. After tools, call again. Emit `ui` for render_ui. Append assistant turn.
  - For sidecar: POST `/api/llm/chat` (new) with same request, parse SSE and forward. Or existing `/api/chat`? The sidecar new proxy can be used. But we can keep existing sidecar stream by calling `/api/chat`? The orchestrator can't import studioApi (circular). Implement fetch to apiUrl("/api/chat")? But then sidecar does everything. We want local data source, so sidecar chat would mutate sidecar data not local. For v1, sidecar LLM proxy with tools executed locally is better. Implement `/api/llm/chat` proxy.
  - `render_ui`: deterministic assistant can emit a simple UI spec? Need catalog schema. Let's inspect ui/protocol and catalog to know spec shape.
