# Agentic ODI [![Open the Living Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20the%20Living%20Studio-F38020?style=for-the-badge&logo=cloudflare&logoColor=white)](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/) [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **[![Experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/Experimental-1e293b?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi)** > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- > **See it live:** **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. > No install required; the interface loads immediately, while live data, chat, and > mutations need the local sidecar ([Deployment](docs/deployment.md)). To run the > full stack yourself, jump to [Quick Start](#quick-start). **Agentic ODI** explores how the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server acts as the "brain" of customer needs — letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in verified, measurable customer outcomes (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores). This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. **Project site:** the site lives at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)**, with a documentation hub at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/)**. It is republished by the `Pages` workflow on every push to `main`. The site is generated from this repository — the MCP tool reference, the connector catalog, and the ODI schema are read from the code that ships, so they cannot drift from it. The CLI reference is hand-written; a test fails when it misses a command. **Hosted Studio:** the experimental Living Studio UI runs at **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. It loads without a backend; live data needs the sidecar tunnel described in [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers Builds. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) with shared tooling at the root. Packages live in `packages/`, runnable services in `apps/`, and deployment assets in `infra/`: | Path | Distribution | Description | |---|---|---| | **`packages/core/`** | `agentic-odi-core` | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), the shared MCP tool contract, and ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`packages/connectors/`** | `agentic-odi-connectors` | Pluggable MCP and REST connectors with presets and an ingest sink. | | **`apps/mcp-server/`** | `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | FastMCP server exposing Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, Evidence, and context tools over HTTP. Persists to SQLite by default. | | **`apps/studio-api/`** | `agentic-odi-studio-api` | FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. Serves config, health, canvas data, local mutations, MCP passthrough, SSE chat, conversation history, and the PM memory store, plus the built SPA. | | **`apps/cli/`** | `agentic-odi-cli` | Typer CLI with interactive chat plus full entity CRUD, `schema`, `connectors`, and local-first (`--backend local`) or remote (`--backend mcp`) data access. | | **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The copilot renders **agent-composed surfaces inline** — scored outcomes, opportunity theses, bet simulations — from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** starts from the PM's ambition, and a local memory records what matters across sessions. | | **`infra/cloudflare/`** | Worker | Worker script for the free-plan Workers Static Assets deployment and sidecar tunnel; its `wrangler.jsonc` lives at the repository root. | | **`scripts/`** | — | Dev launcher, binary build, installer tests. | | **`tests/contract/`** | — | Cross-package MCP contract tests. | See [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) for the dependency graph, data flow, and testing strategy. ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager. ```bash # Install the entire workspace (all five Python projects plus dev tooling) uv sync --all-packages # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together npm --prefix apps/studio run build python scripts/dev.py ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | For hot reload, `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The first time you open the Studio, the tour asks what you want to win: an opportunity you already have in mind, a priority your boss handed you, finding the next opportunity, or pressure-testing a bet. Pick one and the conversation starts there — no form, no framework speech. It still asks for your product and audience when it needs them, and everything you say is optional and skippable. After that it opens as one room: the transcript and the composer never leave the screen. Describe a job or a customer frustration, or type `/` for commands that mirror the CLI. Whatever the thread produces — scored outcomes, an opportunity thesis, a job map, customer evidence — arrives as an inline surface, and a quiet rail above the conversation opens it in a lens that docks beside the thread instead of replacing it. Capture and simulation are conversations too: tell the studio what a customer said, or what bet you are weighing, and it renders the card. Use the bell to **catch up on outcome shifts, simulations, and telemetry signals while you were away**. The studio also remembers the person, not just the canvas. As you talk it notes what matters — your role, the opportunity, business constraints, stakeholders, evidence, how you like to work — and shows each note under **What I know** so you can confirm, correct, add, or forget it. The thread and those notes resume on the next launch. Memory lives in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` (override with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`, or use `:memory:` for tests) and never blocks a reply if it fails. **Forget everything** clears the notes and the thread. The Studio is better with an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support (see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md)), but it does not depend on one: with no model reachable it says so and every job, step, and outcome remains editable by hand. +The hosted Studio also works without any Python sidecar: the browser keeps +canvas data, memory, and a deterministic assistant in IndexedDB (with an +in-memory fallback), and the Cloudflare worker advertises a local-only +capabilities manifest when `SIDECAR_URL` is absent. Enhanced features such as +connectors, MCP, and the sidecar model proxy stay hidden until a local sidecar +is reachable; Settings shows which capabilities are available. + ### Connectors (MCP ↔ Living Studio) Register MCP or REST connectors that the copilot can discover and invoke. - **Where they live**: a shared `connectors.json` registry. Override its location with `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`; by default it is `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`. See [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md). - **In the Living Studio**: open the **Settings** drawer → **Connectors** to list, remove, or add one of the recommended presets (Notion, PostHog, Exa, Linear, GitHub). - **Conversationally**: tell the copilot "use Notion" / "add the GitHub connector". It emits an `add_connector` local tool (handled in-process) that writes the preset to the registry, plus a `connector` SSE event the Studio surfaces as a suggestion chip. Dismissing or accepting the chip also refreshes the list. - **API**: `GET/POST/DELETE /api/connectors`, `GET /api/connectors/catalog`, and `GET /api/connectors/{name}/health` (the catalog honors `?area=` and `?recommended=true`). - **CLI**: `agentic-odi connectors catalog | add | list | health | ingest `. ### When something fails Failures are shown where they happen, not dressed up as empty results. Every HTTP error from the Living Studio sidecar carries one body — `{"error": {"code", "message", "detail", "suggestion", "retryable", "request_id"}}` — and the Studio renders it in place with a **Retry** button that keeps your question. A chat turn always ends with exactly one reply or one error, the canvas shows an invitation when there is nothing yet and a failure panel when the fetch failed, and a broken lens is contained to that lens. Quote the `request_id` when you report a failure: it is echoed on the response header and on every streamed frame, and it is the id in the sidecar's per-turn log line. ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m agentic_odi_cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m agentic_odi_cli --help # show available options and commands python -m agentic_odi_cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi jobs list # Jobs-to-be-Done agentic-odi steps list --job-id agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi evidence list --job-id agentic-odi schema # canonical JSON schema for every entity agentic-odi evaluate "Minimize the time to ship when onboarding" # outcome-format check agentic-odi guidelines # the ODI stage-by-stage guide agentic-odi capabilities # what the assistant can do agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). See the [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md). ### Install the binary Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` The installer symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`. See [Installation](docs/installation.md) for the install layout, updates, and release automation. ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | |---|---| | [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md) | Backends, interactive chat, Jobs/Steps/desired Outcomes/Customer Outcomes/evidence, `connectors`, scoring, environment variables | | [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md) | The MCP ingest connector, presets, and the `Connector` protocol | | [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md) | First-run tour and its flag, local memory and conversation resume, interface, rich inline responses and the UI catalog, run modes, desktop signing and updates, agent-driven testing (`/dev`, `/test`) | | [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md) | Running a local OpenAI-compatible model with tool calling | | [Development](docs/development.md) | Lint, format, type checks, frontend checks, tests and the coverage map | | [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) | Workspace layout, dependency direction, data flow, and testing | | [Installation](docs/installation.md) | Binary install, updater behavior, and release automation | | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) | Project site on GitHub Pages, Hosted Studio and PR preview URLs, the MCP server endpoint, and the free-plan Cloudflare Worker | | [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) | Completed and upcoming milestones | | [Superpowers](docs/superpowers.md) | Pi, OpenCode, and Freebuff integration | Every guide above is also published on the [project site](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/), rendered from these files. The site adds a quick start, a generated MCP tool reference, and the connector catalog. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! This project uses [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) for linting and formatting and [pytest](https://pytest.org/) for tests. Make sure your change passes the [lint, format, and test checks](docs/development.md) before opening a pull request. ## 🦦 Brand Odi the Otter is the mascot of Agentic ODI — a golden-ratio-derived pixel otter who appears in the CLI, the Living Studio, the desktop app icon, the favicon, and this page.     """Proxy a streaming model call so provider keys stay server-side."""
    url = f"{body.base_url.rstrip('/')}/chat/completions"

    async def event_stream():
        headers = {
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
            "Accept": "text/event-stream",
        }
        if body.api_key:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {body.api_key}"
        payload: dict[str, Any] = {
            "model": body.model,
            "messages": [message.model_dump() for message in body.messages],
            "stream": body.stream,
        }
        if body.tools:
            payload["tools"] = body.tools

        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=60.0) as client:
            try:
                async with client.stream(
                    "POST", url, headers=headers, json=payload
                ) as response:
                    if response.status_code >= 400:
                        text = (await response.aread()).decode("utf-8", "replace")
                        yield (
                            "event: error\n"
                            + f"data: {json.dumps({'error': {'code': 'provider_error', 'message': text or f'HTTP {response.status_code}'}})}\n\n"
                        )
                        return
                    async for chunk in response.aiter_bytes():
                        yield chunk.decode("utf-8", "replace")
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                yield (
                    "event: error\n"
                    + f"data: {json.dumps({'error': {'code': 'provider_error', 'message': str(exc)}})}\n\n"
                )

    return StreamingResponse(
        event_stream(),
        media_type="text/event-stream",
        headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"},
    )

flow, and testing strategy.

## Quick Start

**Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package
manager.

```bash
# Install the entire workspace (all five Python projects plus dev tooling)
uv sync --all-packages

# Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together
npm --prefix apps/studio run build
python scripts/dev.py
```

| Service | URL |
|---|---|
| MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp |

- apps/studio/src/bff/: IndexedDB store with in-memory fallback, local ODI CRUD and opportunity scoring, local memory and conversations, capability registry, deterministic assistant, and model-endpoint orchestration.

<skill_content name="writing-plans">
# Skill: writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write implementation plans for an engineer who has not seen this codebase or this spec. Assume they write idiomatic code in the project's language once they know the exact interface and the exact test, and that they will make a reasonable choice wherever the plan leaves one open. What they cannot know is what you decided: which files, which names and signatures, which values from the spec, which tests prove each task. Document those. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Step Granularity

**Each step is one action with a checkable result:**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

## Review Focus

[The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
— one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
owns the code, in that task's own step style.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `function(input: InputType) -> ResultType` in `exact/path/to/file.py`**

One line on the approach when the signature and the test leave a choice
(which library call, which data structure); a code block only for an
algorithm they do not determine.

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## What a Step Contains

A step is done when the implementer can write exactly one reasonable thing
from it. That is the whole requirement: unambiguous, not complete. Each kind
of step carries what makes it unambiguous and nothing more:

- **A test step:** the test's name and its assertions, as code, with the
  spec's exact values in them.
- **A code step:** the exact signature (name, parameters, return type), the
  file it lives in, and the specific values the spec pins. The implementer
  writes the body. A body appears only for an algorithm the signature and
  tests do not determine, or for exact copy the spec fixes.
- **A verification step:** the command to run and the output that means it
  passed.
- **A reference to another task:** that task's Interfaces block says what
  to use; the plan does not repeat that task's code.

A plan is the set of decisions the implementer cannot make alone. A plan
longer than the code it describes has written the code instead. Lines that
decide nothing ("TBD", "handle edge cases", "add appropriate validation",
"write tests for the above", a type or function no task defines) are the
opposite failure, and the self-review catches both.

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Step scan:** Every step must let the implementer write exactly one reasonable thing, and no step may carry more than that: a line that decides nothing is a gap, a function body the signature and tests already determine is a transcript. Fix both.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

**4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.

**5. Proportion:** Compare the plan's length to the spec's. A plan several times longer than the spec it implements is a transcript of the program, not a plan. If code blocks are most of the document, replace bodies with signatures, test names and assertions, and check that each step is still unambiguous.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving and self-reviewing the plan, link it for your human partner
to read. If they have already explicitly supplied an execution method, ask
them to review the plan and confirm it captures what they want; wait for that
review before implementation, then use the preserved method. Otherwise, ask
them to review the plan and choose an execution method before implementation.

**When no execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Which execution approach would you prefer?**

- **Subagent-driven** - A fresh subagent implements each task and a fresh reviewer checks it before the next one starts, then a whole-branch review at the end. Most thorough; costs a fresh context per task and per review.
- **Native** - I implement every task myself in this session, the way this harness runs work, then one fresh reviewer on the most capable model checks the whole branch. Cheapest and fastest; no independent review until the end. Runs well with a mid-tier session model, since the plan carries the design.

**For this plan I recommend <one of the two>, because <one sentence from the plan: how much the tasks depend on each other's interfaces, how many there are, what a shipped mistake would cost>. Does the plan capture what you want, and which approach should we use?"**

**When an execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Does it capture what you want?"**

**If Subagent-driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development

**If Native chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans

parts.text:
Important: main router imports new `TurnNode` from schemas, and schemas has ConversationModel with head_id, TurnModel message_id/parent_id, TurnNode. Our branch schemas lacks those (older). So rebase must take main's schemas and add our new classes at end. Router must take main's full file and append capabilities/llm at end plus imports. Good.

Need inspect main package lock / deps for fake-indexeddb etc; our deps can be added. Main uses assistant-ui packages. Need check main's tsconfig/eslint etc no issue.

Need inspect main's `StudioContext` startup and `turnsToMessages` to know what BFF needs to support: new `fetchConversationTree`, `setConversationHead`, `resolveApproval`, `createConversation`. Our BFF currently lacks these functions, and local conversation model lacks branch fields. Main StudioContext calls `fetchConversationTree` on startup; our local fallback must provide it. It also calls `apiSetConversationHead` on branch switch. If not provided, typecheck will fail. Need plan implement these.

Also main's `streamChat` transforms `request.messages` into history with `id`, `role`, `content`, `parent_id`; our BFF orchestrator currently uses `request.messages` last content, okay but types will require id/parentId. Need add assistant_id, approvals, attachments perhaps. Our BFF should support SSE events expected by main. It emits `tool` statuses "success"/"calling" but main maps status `ok`/`error`/`declined`; "calling"/"success" -> running, so tool chips stay running. Should emit `ok` and `error`, not success/calling. Also tool preview. Need `ui` spec match catalog manifest; our `render_ui` specs likely invalid. """FastAPI app for the Living Studio sidecar."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from pathlib import Path

from agentic_odi_core import ODIService
from agentic_odi_core.remote import StudioError, StudioErrorCode
from agentic_odi_core.repository import Repository
from agentic_odi_core.sqlite_repository import SQLiteRepository
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.approvals import ApprovalRegistry
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.connectors import ConnectorService
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.errors import (
    RequestIdMiddleware,
    StudioHTTPError,
    register_error_handlers,
    request_id_for,
)
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.memory import StudioMemory
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.router import router as studio_router

CORS_ORIGINS = [
    "tauri://localhost",
    "http://tauri.localhost",
    "http://localhost:5173",
    "http://127.0.0.1:5173",
    "http://localhost:8100",
    "http://127.0.0.1:8100",
]

DEFAULT_BACKEND = "local"


def default_spa_dist() -> Path:
    """Resolve the built SPA, preferring an explicit override."""
    configured = os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DIST")
    if configured:
        return Path(configured)
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] / "apps" / "studio" / "dist"


SPA_DIST = default_spa_dist()


def create_app(
    repo: Repository | None = None,
    backend: str | None = None,
    connectors: ConnectorService | None = None,
    memory: StudioMemory | None = None,
) -> FastAPI:
    if repo is None:
        repo = SQLiteRepository()
    service = ODIService(repo)
    # Pending write approvals live for the life of the process: a local sidecar
    # serves one person and has no durable run state to resume into.
    approvals = ApprovalRegistry()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(_app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        yield
        # Nothing may outlive the process waiting on a decision.
        approvals.cancel_all()

    app = FastAPI(
        title="Agentic ODI Studio API",
        openapi_url="/api/openapi.json",
        lifespan=lifespan,
    )
    app.state.service = service
    app.state.backend = backend or os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND") or DEFAULT_BACKEND
    app.state.connectors = connectors or ConnectorService()
    app.state.memory = memory or StudioMemory()
    app.state.approvals = approvals

    app.add_middleware(
        CORSMiddleware,
        allow_origins=CORS_ORIGINS,
        allow_credentials=False,
        allow_methods=["*"],
        allow_headers=["*"],
    )
    app.add_middleware(RequestIdMiddleware)
    register_error_handlers(app)

    @app.get("/health")
    def health() -> dict:
        return {"status": "ok"}

    @app.get("/capabilities")
    def capabilities() -> dict:
        return {"capabilities": app.state.backend}

    app.include_router(studio_router)

    if SPA_DIST.is_dir() and not os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_DISABLE_SPA"):
        assets_dir = SPA_DIST / "assets"
        if assets_dir.is_dir():
            app.mount("/assets", StaticFiles(directory=assets_dir), name="assets")

        @app.get("/{full_path:path}", response_model=None)
        def spa_fallback(request: Request, full_path: str) -> FileResponse | JSONResponse:
            if full_path == "api" or full_path.startswith("api/"):
                raise StudioHTTPError(
                    StudioError(code=StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND, message="Not Found")
                )
            candidate = (SPA_DIST / full_path).resolve()
            if full_path and candidate.is_file() and candidate.is_relative_to(SPA_DIST.resolve()):
                return FileResponse(candidate)
            index = SPA_DIST / "index.html"
            if index.is_file():
                return FileResponse(index)
            error = StudioError(
                code=StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND,
                message="Not Found",
                request_id=request_id_for(request),
            )
            return JSONResponse({"error": error.model_dump(mode="json")}, status_code=404)

    return app

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3

from agentic_odi_core import InMemoryRepository
from agentic_odi_studio_api.app import create_app
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.memory import StudioMemory
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient


def _memory() -> StudioMemory:
    return StudioMemory(":memory:")


def test_turns_keep_the_client_message_ids() -> None:
    memory = _memory()
    conversation = memory.create_conversation()

    memory.append_turn(conversation.id, "user", "list jobs", "m-1", None)
    memory.append_turn(conversation.id, "assistant", "here they are", "m-2", "m-1")

    turns = memory.list_turns(conversation.id)
    assert [(turn.message_id, turn.parent_id) for turn in turns] == [
        ("m-1", None),
        ("m-2", "m-1"),
    ]
    assert memory.get_conversation(conversation.id).head_id == "m-2"  # type: ignore[union-attr]


def test_a_second_answer_to_the_same_question_is_a_sibling() -> None:
    memory = _memory()
    conversation = memory.create_conversation()

    memory.append_turn(conversation.id, "user", "list jobs", "m-1", None)
    memory.append_turn(conversation.id, "assistant", "first", "m-2", "m-1")
    memory.append_turn(conversation.id, "assistant", "second", "m-3", "m-1")

    parents = {
        turn.message_id: turn.parent_id for turn in memory.conversation_tree(conversation.id)
    }
    assert parents == {"m-1": None, "m-2": "m-1", "m-3": "m-1"}

    memory.set_head(conversation.id, "m-2")
    assert memory.get_conversation(conversation.id).head_id == "m-2"  # type: ignore[union-attr]


def test_legacy_rows_are_read_as_a_linear_chain(tmp_path) -> None:
    path = tmp_path / "studio.db"
    connection = sqlite3.connect(path)
    connection.executescript(
        """
        CREATE TABLE conversations (
            id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
            created_at TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
        );
        CREATE TABLE turns (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            conversation_id TEXT NOT NULL, role TEXT NOT NULL,
            content TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL
        );
        INSERT INTO conversations VALUES ('c1', 'Old', 'now', 'now');
        INSERT INTO turns (conversation_id, role, content, created_at)
            VALUES ('c1', 'user', 'hello', 'now');
        INSERT INTO turns (conversation_id, role, content, created_at)
            VALUES ('c1', 'assistant', 'hi', 'now');
        """
    )
    connection.commit()
    connection.close()

    memory = StudioMemory(path)
    turns = memory.conversation_tree("c1")

    assert [(turn.message_id, turn.parent_id) for turn in turns] == [
        ("turn-1", None),
        ("turn-2", "turn-1"),
    ]
    assert memory.get_conversation("c1").head_id is None  # type: ignore[union-attr]


def test_rename_keeps_the_tree() -> None:
    memory = _memory()
    conversation = memory.create_conversation()

    renamed = memory.update_title(conversation.id, "Retention work")

    assert renamed.title == "Retention work"
    assert renamed.head_id is None


def test_the_tree_endpoint_returns_messages_and_the_head() -> None:
    memory = _memory()
    conversation = memory.create_conversation()
    memory.append_turn(conversation.id, "user", "list jobs", "m-1", None)
    memory.append_turn(conversation.id, "assistant", "here they are", "m-2", "m-1")
    app = create_app(repo=InMemoryRepository(), memory=memory)
    client = TestClient(app)

    body = client.get(f"/api/conversations/{conversation.id}/tree").json()

    assert body["conversation"]["id"] == conversation.id
    assert body["head_id"] == "m-2"
    assert [message["id"] for message in body["messages"]] == ["m-1", "m-2"]
    assert body["messages"][1]["parent_id"] == "m-1"
    assert body["messages"][1]["content"] == "here they are"


def test_the_tree_endpoint_reports_an_unknown_conversation() -> None:
    app = create_app(repo=InMemoryRepository(), memory=_memory())
    client = TestClient(app)

    response = client.get("/api/conversations/missing/tree")

    assert response.status_code == 404
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "not_found"


def test_patching_the_head_moves_the_visible_branch() -> None:
    memory = _memory()
    conversation = memory.create_conversation()
    memory.append_turn(conversation.id, "user", "list jobs", "m-1", None)
    memory.append_turn(conversation.id, "assistant", "first", "m-2", "m-1")
    memory.append_turn(conversation.id, "assistant", "second", "m-3", "m-1")
    app = create_app(repo=InMemoryRepository(), memory=memory)
    client = TestClient(app)

    response = client.patch(f"/api/conversations/{conversation.id}", json={"head_id": "m-2"})

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["conversation"]["head_id"] == "m-2"
    assert memory.get_conversation(conversation.id).head_id == "m-2"  # type: ignore[union-attr]


def test_patching_an_unknown_conversation_is_a_404() -> None:
    app = create_app(repo=InMemoryRepository(), memory=_memory())
    client = TestClient(app)

    response = client.patch("/api/conversations/missing", json={"head_id": "m-1"})

    assert response.status_code == 404


def test_an_approval_can_be_answered_through_the_api() -> None:
    app = create_app(repo=InMemoryRepository(), memory=_memory())
    client = TestClient(app)

    response = client.post("/api/approvals/apv_missing", json={"approved": True})

    assert response.status_code == 404
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "not_found"

===== design =====
# Browser BFF for Living Studio

Date: 2026-10-24
Status: Approved

## Problem

The hosted Living Studio depends on a Python sidecar for canvas CRUD, chat, memory,
connectors, and model access. Cloudflare Pages serves the SPA only; without a
reachable sidecar the studio is unusable. We want the hosted studio to be useful
on its own while preserving the richer local experience when a sidecar is running.

## Decision

Add a client-side backend-for-frontend (BFF) inside the SPA. The BFF owns local
data, local memory, capability discovery, and chat orchestration. IndexedDB is the
source of truth for ODI data. The sidecar becomes an optional enhancement provider
for connectors, MCP, CLI integration, and server-side model proxying.

No new hosted server is introduced.

## Architecture

```
React components
  -> StudioContext
    -> StudioBff facade
      -> CapabilityRegistry
      -> LocalDataService  -> LocalStore (IndexedDB, in-memory fallback)
      -> LocalMemoryService ->
      -> ChatOrchestrator -> deterministic local assistant
                           -> browser built-in model (feature detected)
                           -> OpenAI-compatible endpoint (direct fetch)
                           -> sidecar /api/llm/chat (when available)
      -> SidecarEnhancements -> existing /api/* endpoints
```

### Local data

IndexedDB database `agentic-odi-studio` version 1 with stores `meta`, `jobs`,
`steps`, `outcomes`, `observations`, `conversations`, and `turns`. A `LocalStore`
interface isolates persistence so tests use `fake-indexeddb` and browsers without
IndexedDB fall back to an in-memory store for the session.

Domain behavior mirrors `packages/core`: job/step/outcome CRUD, insertion order,
opportunity score `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`, step cascade
on job delete, outcome cascade on step delete, and input validation.

### Capabilities

`CapabilityRegistry` probes and exposes:

| Capability | Availability |
| --- | --- |
| `local-data` | always |
| `local-memory` | always |
| `deterministic-assistant` | always |
| `browser-model` | feature detected |
| `endpoint-model` | configured endpoint URL + model |
| `sidecar-llm` | sidecar capability probe |
| `sidecar-connectors` | sidecar capability probe |
| `sidecar-mcp` | sidecar capability probe |
| `sidecar-import` | sidecar capability probe |

Enhanced controls are hidden when unavailable. Settings shows a compact status
list and the chat empty state links to it. Toasts/hints explain that running the
local sidecar unlocks connectors and MCP.

### Assistant and memory

`ChatOrchestrator` streams events in the existing SSE shape (`message`, `chunk`,
`tool`, `tool_result`, `ui`, `done`, `error`) so the current conversation UI keeps
working. The deterministic assistant answers common questions about the canvas
and supports core jobs/steps/outcomes plus `remember` and `render_ui`. External
models use the OpenAI-compatible tool loop. Sidecar chat remains available as an
enhancement and for tools that only exist server-side.

Conversation history and observations are stored locally. A one-time import from
the sidecar fills the local store only when it is empty. JSON workspace export and
import are provided; automatic replication and E2EE are deliberately deferred.

### Sidecar

The existing `/api/chat` endpoint is unchanged for other clients. Add:

- `POST /api/llm/chat`: streaming OpenAI-compatible proxy that keeps provider keys
  server-side and avoids browser CORS restrictions.
- `GET /api/capabilities`: capability manifest used by the SPA probe.
- Existing CRUD/memory endpoints remain for import and enhancement use.

### Hosted worker

`infra/cloudflare/worker.ts` returns a local-only capability manifest with status
200 when `SIDECAR_URL` is absent. CSP `connect-src` is built from `LLM_ORIGINS`
(defaults limited to localhost plus curated providers) so direct browser model
calls are allowed only where configured.

## Risks

- IndexedDB is origin-scoped. Hosted and desktop origins do not share data; export
  is available for moving a workspace.
- Browser built-in LLM APIs are not universally available. Detection must be
  conservative and the UI must hide the option when absent.
- Direct provider calls expose the user's key to the browser by design; the
  sidecar proxy is the recommended path when available.
- No automatic sync means local and sidecar data can diverge. The one-time import
  and explicit export/import make the boundary visible.

## Acceptance

- The hosted SPA can create and edit canvas data with no sidecar.
- Local data survives reload in an IndexedDB-capable browser.
- The deterministic assistant can read and mutate the canvas.
- Enhanced features stay hidden unless detected; Settings reports why.
- Existing sidecar behavior and Python tests remain green.
- `npm --prefix apps/studio run lint|typecheck|test|build` and `uv run pytest` pass.
===== plan =====
# Browser BFF implementation plan

Date: 2026-10-24
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-24-browser-bff-design.md`

## Task 1: Local persistence and domain parity

- Add `idb` and `fake-indexeddb`.
- Create `apps/studio/src/bff/store/` with a `LocalStore` interface, IndexedDB
  implementation, and in-memory fallback.
- Create `apps/studio/src/bff/data/localDataService.ts` mirroring the Python ODI
  service: canvas read model, job/step/outcome CRUD, scoring, validation, and
  cascading deletes.
- Tests: store durability with `fake-indexeddb`, score math, insertion order,
  cascade behavior, and validation.

## Task 2: Capabilities and UI integration

- Create `CapabilityRegistry` with local, browser-model, endpoint-model, and
  sidecar probes.
- Add `StudioBff` facade.
- Route `StudioContext` canvas CRUD through `StudioBff` instead of the sidecar.
- Add capability status to Settings, hide enhanced controls when unavailable, and
  update the offline notice.
- Add a `localAssistant` feature flag.
- Tests: registry detection and Settings rendering.

## Task 3: Local assistant and memory

- Create `LocalMemoryService` for observations, conversations, turns, and prompt
  context.
- Create `ChatOrchestrator`: deterministic assistant, browser model, endpoint
  model, and sidecar proxy selection.
- Implement local core tools (`get_canvas`, job/step/outcome CRUD,
  `compute_opportunity`, `evaluate_outcome`, `remember`, `render_ui`).
- Stream the existing SSE event shape.
- Tests: deterministic tool calls, memory writes, event ordering, model selection.

## Task 4: Sidecar continuity and enhancements

- Add `GET /api/capabilities` and `POST /api/llm/chat` to the sidecar.
- Add one-time import from sidecar when local storage is empty.
- Add workspace JSON export/import.
- Keep existing `/api/chat` unchanged.
- Tests: capability manifest, proxy request shape, import/export round trip.

## Task 5: Hosted hardening

- Worker returns a local-only capability manifest when `SIDECAR_URL` is absent.
- Build CSP `connect-src` from `LLM_ORIGINS`.
- Update `wrangler.jsonc` documentation.
- Tests: worker response and CSP construction.

## Task 6: Documentation and verification

- Update `README.md`, `docs/living-studio.md`, `docs/deployment.md`, and
  `docs/architecture/*`.
- Regenerate `apps/studio/openapi.json` and `src/api/schema.d.ts`.
- Run lint, typecheck, unit tests, build, and `uv run pytest`.
- Push branch and open a PR with a non-empty body; wait for CI.

interface isolates persistence so tests use `fake-indexeddb` and browsers without
IndexedDB fall back to an in-memory store for the session.

Domain behavior mirrors `packages/core`: job/step/outcome CRUD, insertion order,
opportunity score `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`, step cascade
on job delete, outcome cascade on step delete, and input validation.

### Capabilities

`CapabilityRegistry` probes and exposes:

| Capability | Availability |
| --- | --- |
| `local-data` | always |
| `local-memory` | always |
| `deterministic-assistant` | always |
| `browser-model` | feature detected |
| `endpoint-model` | configured endpoint URL + model |
| `sidecar-llm` | sidecar capability probe |
| `sidecar-connectors` | sidecar capability probe |
| `sidecar-mcp` | sidecar capability probe |
| `sidecar-import` | sidecar capability probe |

Enhanced controls are hidden when unavailable. Settings shows a compact status
list and the chat empty state links to it. Toasts/hints explain that running the
local sidecar unlocks connectors and MCP.

### Assistant and memory

`ChatOrchestrator` streams events in the existing SSE shape (`message`, `chunk`,
`tool`, `tool_result`, `ui`, `done`, `error`) so the current conversation UI keeps
working. The deterministic assistant answers common questions about the canvas
and supports core jobs/steps/outcomes plus `remember` and `render_ui`. External
models use the OpenAI-compatible tool loop. Sidecar chat remains available as an
enhancement and for tools that only exist server-side.

Conversation history and observations are stored locally. A one-time import from
the sidecar fills the local store only when it is empty. JSON workspace export and
import are provided; automatic replication and E2EE are deliberately deferred.

### Sidecar

The existing `/api/chat` endpoint is unchanged for other clients. Add:

- `POST /api/llm/chat`: streaming OpenAI-compatible proxy that keeps provider keys
  server-side and avoids browser CORS restrictions.
- `GET /api/capabilities`: capability manifest used by the SPA probe.
- Existing CRUD/memory endpoints remain for import and enhancement use.

### Hosted worker

`infra/cloudflare/worker.ts` returns a local-only capability manifest with status
200 when `SIDECAR_URL` is absent. CSP `connect-src` is built from `LLM_ORIGINS`
(defaults limited to localhost plus curated providers) so direct browser model
calls are allowed only where configured.

## Risks

- IndexedDB is origin-scoped. Hosted and desktop origins do not share data; export
  is available for moving a workspace.
- Browser built-in LLM APIs are not universally available. Detection must be
  conservative and the UI must hide the option when absent.
- Direct provider calls expose the user's key to the browser by design; the
  sidecar proxy is the recommended path when available.
- No automatic sync means local and sidecar data can diverge. The one-time import
  and explicit export/import make the boundary visible.

## Acceptance

- The hosted SPA can create and edit canvas data with no sidecar.
- Local data survives reload in an IndexedDB-capable browser.
- The deterministic assistant can read and mutate the canvas.
- Enhanced features stay hidden unless detected; Settings reports why.
- Existing sidecar behavior and Python tests remain green.
- `npm --prefix apps/studio run lint|typecheck|test|build` and `uv run pytest` pass.

- Update BFF types to new ChatMessage ids/parents, ConversationTurn message_id/parent_id, Conversation head_id, ChatStreamRequest attachments/approvals/assistant_id.

 # Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails
 
 This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.
 
 > **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `docs/reference/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.
 
 ---
 
 ## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails
 
 This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.
 
 ### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?
 
 ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.
 
 ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done
 
 - A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
 - A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
 - **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
 - ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes
 
 - **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
 - Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
 - **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):
 
   > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`
 
   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
   - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
   - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.
 
 - **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)
 
 - All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
   1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
   2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
   3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
   4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
   5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
   6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
   7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
   8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs
 
 - **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
 - ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)
 
 - Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
   - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
   - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?
 
 - **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):
 
   ```
   Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
   ```
 
 - **Interpretation**:
   - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
   - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
   - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.
 
 - **Agent rule**: Always compute and surface the opportunity score when both `importance` and `satisfaction` are provided. Highlight outcomes scoring **> 10** as the highest priority innovation targets. Use `get_outcomes(job_id)` to review the full opportunity landscape.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 5: Outcome-Based Market Segmentation
 
 - ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
 - Segments can be:
   - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
   - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
   - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value
 
 - **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy
 
 Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:
 
 | Strategy | When to use |
 |---|---|
 | **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
 | **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
 | **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |
 
 - **Agent rule**: When the opportunity landscape is clear (outcomes scored, segments identified), guide the user to select a strategy path and align their innovation roadmap accordingly.
 
 ---
 
 ### ⚠️ ODI Behavioral Guardrails for the Agent
 
 These are absolute constraints the agent must respect:
 
 | DO | DON'T |
 |---|---|
 | Always start by defining or confirming the Job-to-be-Done | Jump to solutions, features, or product ideas before the job is defined |
 | Guide outcome statements with the correct format | Accept vague or solution-framed statements as valid outcomes |
 | Compute opportunity scores when importance + satisfaction are available | Skip scoring or calculate it incorrectly |
 | Reference the Universal Job Map when decomposing jobs | Invent arbitrary step structures disconnected from the 8 universal stages |
 | Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments | Use demographics or assumptions to segment the market |
 | Treat outcomes as stable, measurable success metrics | Confuse outcomes with features, preferences, or solutions |
 | Call `get_odi_framework_guidelines` when stage guidance is needed | Guess at which stage comes next |

+  become a second source of truth.
+- **The SSE contract stays additive.** The sidecar is a Python tool loop; it is
+  not migrating to Vercel's AI SDK stream protocol. New capability arrives as a
+  new event (`reasoning`, `source`, `approval`, `ui`, …) or a new opt-in request
+  field, and a client that sends neither must see the old stream unchanged.
+- **The ODI catalog stays ours.** Generated surfaces travel as assistant-ui
+  `data-*` parts and render through `UiRenderer`. assistant-ui's generic
+  generative-UI vocabulary is not a replacement for the server-validated catalog.
+- **No fabricated provenance.** A source names what a turn actually read; a part
+  the converter does not understand is dropped, never printed as JSON.
+- **Approvals gate writes, not reads.** `approvals: true` pauses mutating tools
+  only; the gate is in-process, single-user, timeout-bound, and resolving a gate
+  twice must not run a tool twice.
+- **Voice is a seam, not a feature.** It is deliberately deferred: `adapters.dictation`
+  plus `ComposerPrimitive.Dictate`, no backend change. Do not ship a microphone
+  that only works in the browser shell.
+- **Keep it honest in the docs.** A capability that lands here is described in
+  `docs/living-studio.md` → *The conversation runtime*, with its test in
+  `docs/development.md`, in the same change.
+
+### 6. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
 - **First-Class Documentation**: Treat tests as living documentation that demonstrate how features work while protecting against regressions.
 - **Speed & Isolation**: Tests must be fast (< 1s) and self-contained. Use `@pytest.mark.integration` or `@pytest.mark.client_process` for slower, integration, or resource-dependent tests.
 - **Structure**: This repo is a uv workspace. Mirror each project's code structure in its own `tests/` directory (e.g., `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py` -> `apps/mcp-server/tests/test_server_tools.py`, `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/mcp/connector.py` -> `packages/connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py`).
 - **Atomic Tests**: Each test must verify exactly one specific behavior with clear intent in test names and assertions. Avoid multi-behavior tests.
 - **In-Memory Testing (Preferred)**: Favor testing functionality deterministically by passing the `FastMCP` server directly into the `Client(server)` instance. This runs in-memory without network overhead for deterministic and lightning-fast execution.
 - **Transport Testing (When Needed)**: For HTTP/SSE network transport tests, prefer the isolated in-process `fastmcp.utilities.tests.run_server_async(server)` context manager over subprocess testing (which uses `run_server_in_process` and is slower to debug).
 - **Data Assertions**: Utilize `inline-snapshot` (`snapshot()`) for assessing complex data structures like tool API JSON schemas or expected responses.

--- .github/actions/pr-risk/score.sh	
+++ .github/actions/pr-risk/score.sh	
@@ -0,0 +1,186 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+#
+# score.sh — Native GitHub Action PR risk classifier.
+#
+# Evaluates a pull request diff across three factors and applies a single,
+# mutually exclusive risk label. Runs entirely on ubuntu-latest with git + gh
+# (both preinstalled on GitHub-hosted runners). Zero external SaaS, zero API
+# keys, zero PR comments.
+#
+# Factors (0-100 score):
+#   1. File & line churn        -> 0-30 points
+#   2. Critical path override   -> forces danger zone (>= 51)
+#   3. Test delta               -> +20 if source changed without test files
+#
+# Tiers:
+#   <= 20  -> safe to merge     (🟢)
+#   21-50  -> needs a look      (🟡)
+#   >= 51  -> danger zone       (🔴)
+#
+# Env required: GITHUB_TOKEN, BASE_SHA, HEAD_SHA, PR_NUMBER, REPO
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Configuration
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+readonly RISK_LABELS=("safe to merge" "needs a look" "danger zone")
+readonly CRITICAL_PREFIXES=("auth/" "migrations/" "billing/" "infra/" ".github/workflows/")
+readonly PROTECTED_FILES_FILE=".ci/protected-files.txt"
+
+# Score thresholds
+readonly CHURN_FILES_MAX=10      # points
+readonly CHURN_LINES_MAX=20      # points
+readonly CHURN_LINES_CAP=400     # lines at which line-points saturate
+readonly TEST_DELTA_POINTS=20
+readonly DANGER_FLOOR=51
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Helpers
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# Returns 0 (true) if $1 is a test file: *.test.*, *.spec.*, or under tests/
+is_test_file() {
+  local f="$1"
+  [[ "${f}" == *.test.* || "${f}" == *.spec.* ]] && return 0
+  [[ "${f}" == tests/* || "${f}" == */tests/* ]] && return 0
+  return 1
+}
+
+# Returns 0 (true) if $1 is source code worth test coverage (excludes docs,
+# configs, static assets, lockfiles, etc.). Test delta only fires on these.
+is_source_file() {
+  local f="$1"
+  local ext="${f##*.}"
+  case "${ext}" in
+    py|ts|tsx|js|jsx|go|rs|rb|java|c|cpp|h|hpp|cs|php|swift|kt|scala|r|m|mm|sh|bash|zsh|tf|vue|dart|lua|ex|exs|erl|hs|ml|clj|cljs|sql|graphql|proto) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  local base="${f##*/}"
+  case "${base}" in
+    Dockerfile|dockerfile|Makefile|makefile|Gemfile|Rakefile|Vagrantfile|BUILD|BUILD.bazel|WORKSPACE|configure|Configure) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Gather diff between base and head
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# All changed files (Added / Copied / Modified / Deleted)
+CHANGED_FILES="$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMD "${BASE_SHA}" "${HEAD_SHA}" || true)"
+
+# Shortstat for churn counts
+STAT="$(git diff --shortstat "${BASE_SHA}" "${HEAD_SHA}" || true)"
+
+FILES_CHANGED_COUNT=0
+LINES_ADDED=0
+LINES_DELETED=0
+if [[ -n "${STAT}" ]]; then
+  FILES_CHANGED_COUNT="$(printf '%s' "${STAT}" | grep -oE '[0-9]+ file' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo 0)"
+  LINES_ADDED="$(printf '%s' "${STAT}" | grep -oE '[0-9]+ insertion' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo 0)"
+  LINES_DELETED="$(printf '%s' "${STAT}" | grep -oE '[0-9]+ deletion' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo 0)"
+fi
+[[ -z "${FILES_CHANGED_COUNT}" ]] && FILES_CHANGED_COUNT=0
+[[ -z "${LINES_ADDED}" ]] && LINES_ADDED=0
+[[ -z "${LINES_DELETED}" ]] && LINES_DELETED=0
+readonly TOTAL_LINES=$((LINES_ADDED + LINES_DELETED))
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Factor 1: File & line churn (0-30)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+score=0
+
+# Files changed: 1 point per file, capped at CHURN_FILES_MAX
+if [[ "${FILES_CHANGED_COUNT}" -ge "${CHURN_FILES_MAX}" ]]; then
+  churn_files="${CHURN_FILES_MAX}"
+else
+  churn_files="${FILES_CHANGED_COUNT}"
+fi
+score=$((score + churn_files))
+
+# Lines changed: linear up to CHURN_LINES_MAX at CHURN_LINES_CAP lines
+if [[ "${TOTAL_LINES}" -ge "${CHURN_LINES_CAP}" ]]; then
+  churn_lines="${CHURN_LINES_MAX}"
+else
+  churn_lines=$((TOTAL_LINES * CHURN_LINES_MAX / CHURN_LINES_CAP))
+  [[ "${churn_lines}" -gt "${CHURN_LINES_MAX}" ]] && churn_lines="${CHURN_LINES_MAX}"
+fi
+score=$((score + churn_lines))
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Factor 2: Critical path override (blast radius)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+critical_touch=0
+
+while IFS= read -r f; do
+  [[ -z "${f}" ]] && continue
+  for prefix in "${CRITICAL_PREFIXES[@]}"; do
+    if [[ "${f}" == "${prefix}"* ]]; then
+      critical_touch=1
+      break 2
+    fi
+  done
+done <<< "${CHANGED_FILES}"
+
+# Deletions of protected CI/site files also count as critical.
+if [[ -f "${PROTECTED_FILES_FILE}" && -n "${CHANGED_FILES}" ]]; then
+  while IFS= read -r f; do
+    [[ -z "${f}" ]] && continue
+    # Only consider deletions: a file in the diff that no longer exists at HEAD
+    if ! git cat-file -e "${HEAD_SHA}:${f}" 2>/dev/null; then
+      while IFS= read -r p; do
+        [[ -z "${p}" || "${p}" == \#* ]] && continue
+        if [[ "${f}" == "${p}" ]]; then
+          critical_touch=1
+          break 2
+        fi
+      done < "${PROTECTED_FILES_FILE}"
+    fi
+  done <<< "${CHANGED_FILES}"
+fi
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Factor 3: Test delta (+20 if source changed without test files)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+source_changed=0
+test_changed=0
+
+while IFS= read -r f; do
+  [[ -z "${f}" ]] && continue
+  if is_test_file "${f}"; then
+    test_changed=1
+  elif is_source_file "${f}"; then
+    source_changed=1
+  fi
+done <<< "${CHANGED_FILES}"
+
+if [[ "${source_changed}" -eq 1 && "${test_changed}" -eq 0 ]]; then
+  score=$((score + TEST_DELTA_POINTS))
+fi
+
+# Apply critical-path floor
+if [[ "${critical_touch}" -eq 1 && "${score}" -lt "${DANGER_FLOOR}" ]]; then
+  score="${DANGER_FLOOR}"
+fi
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Determine tier (mutually exclusive)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+if [[ "${score}" -le 20 ]]; then
+  tier="safe to merge"
+elif [[ "${score}" -le 50 ]]; then
+  tier="needs a look"
+else
+  tier="danger zone"
+fi
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Label hygiene: remove all stale risk labels, then apply the current tier.
+# No PR comments are posted (silent execution).
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+for label in "${RISK_LABELS[@]}"; do
+  gh pr edit "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${REPO}" --remove-label "${label}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+done
+gh pr edit "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${REPO}" --add-label "${tier}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+
+echo "PR risk score: ${score}/100 -> ${tier}"

+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
+    branches: [main]
+
+concurrency:
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}

+

+  pull-requests: write
+  checks: write
+
+defaults:

+
+jobs:

+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout PR branch (full history for diffs)

+        with:
