# Agentic ODI [![Open the Living Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20the%20Living%20Studio-F38020?style=for-the-badge&logo=cloudflare&logoColor=white)](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/) [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **[![Experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/Experimental-1e293b?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi)** > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- > **See it live:** **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. > No install required; the interface loads immediately, while live data, chat, and > mutations need the local sidecar ([Deployment](docs/deployment.md)). To run the > full stack yourself, jump to [Quick Start](#quick-start). **Agentic ODI** explores how the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server acts as the "brain" of customer needs — letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in verified, measurable customer outcomes (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores). This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. **Project site:** the site lives at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)**, with a documentation hub at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/)**. It is republished by the `Pages` workflow on every push to `main`. The site is generated from this repository — the MCP tool reference, the connector catalog, and the ODI schema are read from the code that ships, so they cannot drift from it. The CLI reference is hand-written; a test fails when it misses a command. **Hosted Studio:** the experimental Living Studio UI runs at **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. It loads without a backend; live data needs the sidecar tunnel described in [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers Builds. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) with shared tooling at the root. Packages live in `packages/`, runnable services in `apps/`, and deployment assets in `infra/`: | Path | Distribution | Description | |---|---|---| | **`packages/core/`** | `agentic-odi-core` | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), the shared MCP tool contract, and ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`packages/connectors/`** | `agentic-odi-connectors` | Pluggable MCP and REST connectors with presets and an ingest sink. | | **`apps/mcp-server/`** | `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | FastMCP server exposing Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, Evidence, and context tools over HTTP. Persists to SQLite by default. | | **`apps/studio-api/`** | `agentic-odi-studio-api` | FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. Serves config, health, canvas data, local mutations, MCP passthrough, SSE chat, conversation history, and the PM memory store, plus the built SPA. | | **`apps/cli/`** | `agentic-odi-cli` | Typer CLI with interactive chat plus full entity CRUD, `schema`, `connectors`, and local-first (`--backend local`) or remote (`--backend mcp`) data access. | -| **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The copilot renders **agent-composed surfaces inline** — scored outcomes, opportunity theses, bet simulations — from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** starts from the PM's ambition, and a local memory records what matters across sessions. | +| **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The conversation runs on **assistant-ui** — streaming, reasoning, tool calls, approvals, sources, attachments, branches, and suggestions are the library's runtime; the ODI intelligence and the **agent-composed surfaces** (scored outcomes, opportunity theses, bet simulations) are ours, from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** starts from the PM's ambition, and a local memory records what matters across sessions. | | **`infra/cloudflare/`** | Worker | Worker script for the free-plan Workers Static Assets deployment and sidecar tunnel; its `wrangler.jsonc` lives at the repository root. | | **`scripts/`** | — | Dev launcher, binary build, installer tests. | | **`tests/contract/`** | — | Cross-package MCP contract tests. | See [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) for the dependency graph, data flow, and testing strategy. ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager. ```bash # Install the entire workspace (all five Python projects plus dev tooling) uv sync --all-packages # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together npm --prefix apps/studio run build python scripts/dev.py ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | For hot reload, `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The first time you open the Studio, the tour asks what you want to win: an opportunity you already have in mind, a priority your boss handed you, finding the next opportunity, or pressure-testing a bet. Pick one and the conversation starts there — no form, no framework speech. It still asks for your product and audience when it needs them, and everything you say is optional and skippable. After that it opens as one room: the transcript and the composer never leave the screen. Describe a job or a customer frustration, or type `/` for commands that mirror the CLI. Whatever the thread produces — scored outcomes, an opportunity thesis, a job map, customer evidence — arrives as an inline surface, and a quiet rail above the conversation opens it in a lens that docks beside the thread instead of replacing it. Capture and simulation are conversations too: tell the studio what a customer said, or what bet you are weighing, and it renders the card. Use the bell to **catch up on outcome shifts, simulations, and telemetry signals while you were away**. +The thread behaves like a real assistant surface, not a chat box. Replies stream; +reasoning arrives as a collapsed disclosure rather than prose; each tool call is a +trace chip with the source the turn actually read; a write to your data pauses for +a **Yes/No** before it runs; text and image attachments ride along with the turn; +and any reply can be edited or regenerated as a **branch** you step through with +`‹ 2 of 3 ›`. Starter suggestions change with the canvas. The runtime underneath +is [assistant-ui](https://www.assistant-ui.com); the ODI surfaces, the catalog, +and the sidecar contract stay ours. + The studio also remembers the person, not just the canvas. As you talk it notes what matters — your role, the opportunity, business constraints, stakeholders, evidence, how you like to work — and shows each note under **What I know** so you can confirm, correct, add, or forget it. The thread and those notes resume on the next launch. Memory lives in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` (override with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`, or use `:memory:` for tests) and never blocks a reply if it fails. **Forget everything** clears the notes and the thread. The Studio is better with an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support (see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md)), but it does not depend on one: with no model reachable it says so and every job, step, and outcome remains editable by hand. The hosted Studio also works without any Python sidecar: the browser keeps canvas data, memory, and a deterministic assistant in IndexedDB (with an in-memory fallback), and the Cloudflare worker advertises a local-only capabilities manifest when `SIDECAR_URL` is absent. Enhanced features such as connectors, MCP, and the sidecar model proxy stay hidden until a local sidecar is reachable; Settings shows which capabilities are available. ### Connectors (MCP ↔ Living Studio) Register MCP or REST connectors that the copilot can discover and invoke. - **Where they live**: a shared `connectors.json` registry. Override its location with `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`; by default it is `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`. See [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md). - **In the Living Studio**: open the **Settings** drawer → **Connectors** to list, remove, or add one of the recommended presets (Notion, PostHog, Exa, Linear, GitHub). - **Conversationally**: tell the copilot "use Notion" / "add the GitHub connector". It emits an `add_connector` local tool (handled in-process) that writes the preset to the registry, plus a `connector` SSE event the Studio surfaces as a suggestion chip. Dismissing or accepting the chip also refreshes the list. - **API**: `GET/POST/DELETE /api/connectors`, `GET /api/connectors/catalog`, and `GET /api/connectors/{name}/health` (the catalog honors `?area=` and `?recommended=true`). - **CLI**: `agentic-odi connectors catalog | add | list | health | ingest `. ### When something fails Failures are shown where they happen, not dressed up as empty results. Every HTTP error from the Living Studio sidecar carries one body — `{"error": {"code", "message", "detail", "suggestion", "retryable", "request_id"}}` — and the Studio renders it in place with a **Retry** button that keeps your question. A chat turn always ends with exactly one reply or one error, the canvas shows an invitation when there is nothing yet and a failure panel when the fetch failed, and a broken lens is contained to that lens. Quote the `request_id` when you report a failure: it is echoed on the response header and on every streamed frame, and it is the id in the sidecar's per-turn log line. ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m agentic_odi_cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m agentic_odi_cli --help # show available options and commands python -m agentic_odi_cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi jobs list # Jobs-to-be-Done agentic-odi steps list --job-id agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi evidence list --job-id agentic-odi schema # canonical JSON schema for every entity agentic-odi evaluate "Minimize the time to ship when onboarding" # outcome-format check agentic-odi guidelines # the ODI stage-by-stage guide agentic-odi capabilities # what the assistant can do agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). See the [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md). ### Install the binary Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` The installer symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`. See [Installation](docs/installation.md) for the install layout, updates, and release automation. ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | |---|---| | [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md) | Backends, interactive chat, Jobs/Steps/desired Outcomes/Customer Outcomes/evidence, `connectors`, scoring, environment variables | | [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md) | The MCP ingest connector, presets, and the `Connector` protocol | -| [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md) | First-run tour and its flag, local memory and conversation resume, interface, rich inline responses and the UI catalog, run modes, desktop signing and updates, agent-driven testing (`/dev`, `/test`) | +| [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md) | First-run tour and its flag, the assistant-ui conversation runtime, approvals, branches, attachments, local memory and conversation resume, interface, rich inline responses and the UI catalog, run modes, desktop signing and updates, agent-driven testing (`/dev`, `/test`) | | [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md) | Running a local OpenAI-compatible model with tool calling | | [Development](docs/development.md) | Lint, format, type checks, frontend checks, tests and the coverage map | | [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) | Workspace layout, dependency direction, data flow, and testing | | [Installation](docs/installation.md) | Binary install, updater behavior, and release automation | | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) | Project site on GitHub Pages, Hosted Studio and PR preview URLs, the MCP server endpoint, and the free-plan Cloudflare Worker | | [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) | Completed and upcoming milestones | | [Superpowers](docs/superpowers.md) | Pi, OpenCode, and Freebuff integration | Every guide above is also published on the [project site](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/), rendered from these files. The site adds a quick start, a generated MCP tool reference, and the connector catalog. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! This project uses [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) for linting and formatting and [pytest](https://pytest.org/) for tests. Make sure your change passes the [lint, format, and test checks](docs/development.md) before opening a pull request. +## PR Risk Classification + +Every pull request is automatically classified by the +[PR Risk Classification](.github/workflows/pr-risk.yml) workflow, which runs on +`ubuntu-latest` at $0 cost with zero external dependencies. It scores the diff +(0–100) across three factors and applies a single, mutually exclusive label: + +| Label | Meaning | Score | +|---|---|---| +| `safe to merge` | Low risk — small diff, docs-only, or tested source code | ≤ 20 | +| `needs a look` | Medium risk — standard feature work or missing test updates | 21–50 | +| `danger zone` | High risk — critical path (auth, migrations, billing, infra, workflows) or protected-file deletion | ≥ 51 | + +Scoring factors: +- **File & line churn** — files changed and lines added/deleted (0–30 points). +- **Critical path override** — touching `auth/`, `migrations/`, `billing/`, + `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, or deleting a file in + `.ci/protected-files.txt` forces the danger zone. +- **Test delta** — source code changed without a corresponding + `*.test.*`/`*.spec.*`/`tests/**` file adds 20 points. + +The workflow is silent: it updates labels only and never posts PR comments. + ## 🦦 Brand Odi the Otter is the mascot of Agentic ODI — a golden-ratio-derived pixel otter who appears in the CLI, the Living Studio, the desktop app icon, the favicon, and this page.  ) -> None:
     """Check for or apply CLI updates."""
     if check:

         if latest is None:
             typer.echo(f"Already up to date (v{__version__}).")
         else:
             typer.echo(f"Update available: v{latest} - run 'odi update' to install.")
         return
 
     if not paths.is_frozen():
         typer.echo("This is a source install; use your package manager to update.")
         return
 
     target = version.lstrip("v") if version else update.latest_release(__version__)
     if target is None:
         if force:
             target = __version__
         else:
             typer.echo(f"Already up to date (v{__version__}).")
             return
 
     try:
         with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="odi-update-") as tmp:
             archive = update.download(target, Path(tmp))
             digest = hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
             update.perform_update(target, archive, digest, paths.install_root())
     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
         typer.echo(f"Update failed: {exc}", err=True)
         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from exc

+"""Long tools report progress so the Studio can stop looking hung."""

+
+import json
+from typing import Any, cast

+import pytest
+from agentic_odi_mcp_server.mcp_server import mcp
+from fastmcp import Client

+
+async def _collect_progress(client: Client, tool: str, arguments: dict) -> tuple[object, list]:
+    events: list[tuple[float, float | None, str | None]] = []
+
+    async def on_progress(progress: float, total: float | None, message: str | None) -> None:
+        events.append((progress, total, message))
+
+    result = await client.call_tool(tool, arguments, progress_handler=on_progress)
+    return result, events
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_evaluate_outcome_reports_progress_before_returning() -> None:
+    async with Client(mcp) as client:

+            "evaluate_outcome",
+            {"statement": "Minimize the time to ship when the build is green"},
+        )
+
+    assert json.loads(cast(Any, result).content[0].text)["valid"] is True
+    assert events
+    assert events[-1][0] == events[-1][1]
+    assert events[-1][2] == "Evaluation complete"
+
+

+"""In-process approval gates for mutating tool calls.
+
+A mutating MCP tool (``add_job``, ``update_outcome``, …) pauses the streaming
+turn until the person in front of the Studio says yes or no. The gate is a
+process-local registry of pending futures: the SSE generator awaits one, and
+``POST /api/approvals/{id}`` resolves it.
+
+This is deliberately the smallest thing that is honest. The sidecar serves one
+local user over one loopback socket; it has no durable job state and no worker
+pool, so a gate that lives in memory is the whole requirement. Every gate has a
+timeout and every gate resolves once, so a turn can never hang and a double
+click can never run a tool twice.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import threading
+import uuid
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+
+#: A person deciding whether the agent may write to their data deserves longer
+#: than a network timeout, but the turn must still end on its own.
+DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300.0
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ApprovalRequest:
+    """One pending decision, described well enough for the UI to ask."""
+
+    id: str
+    tool_call_id: str
+    name: str
+    arguments: dict[str, object]
+    prompt: str
+    created_at: str = field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat())
+
+    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
+        return {
+            "id": self.id,
+            "tool_call_id": self.tool_call_id,
+            "name": self.name,
+            "arguments": self.arguments,
+            "prompt": self.prompt,
+            "created_at": self.created_at,
+        }
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ApprovalDecision:
+    approved: bool
+    reason: str = ""
+
+
+class ApprovalNotFoundError(KeyError):
+    """No pending gate has that id, or it already resolved."""
+
+
+class ApprovalRegistry:
+    """Pending approval gates, keyed by the id the client answers with."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()
+        self._pending: dict[str, asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision]] = {}
+
+    def open(
+        self,
+        *,
+        tool_call_id: str,
+        name: str,
+        arguments: dict[str, object],
+        prompt: str,
+    ) -> tuple[ApprovalRequest, asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision]]:
+        """Register a gate and return its description and the future to await."""
+        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
+        request = ApprovalRequest(
+            id=f"apv_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}",
+            tool_call_id=tool_call_id,
+            name=name,
+            arguments=arguments,
+            prompt=prompt,
+        )
+        future: asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision] = loop.create_future()
+        with self._lock:
+            self._pending[request.id] = future
+        return request, future
+
+    def resolve(self, approval_id: str, decision: ApprovalDecision) -> None:
+        """Answer a pending gate. Raises when the gate is unknown or already closed."""
+        with self._lock:
+            future = self._pending.pop(approval_id, None)
+        if future is None or future.done():
+            raise ApprovalNotFoundError(approval_id)
+        future.set_result(decision)
+
+    def discard(self, approval_id: str) -> None:
+        """Forget a gate without answering it (the turn ended first)."""
+        with self._lock:
+            self._pending.pop(approval_id, None)
+
+    def cancel_all(self) -> None:
+        """Drop every pending gate. Called when the sidecar shuts down."""
+        with self._lock:
+            pending = list(self._pending.items())
+            self._pending.clear()
+        for _approval_id, future in pending:
+            if not future.done():
+                future.cancel()
+
+    @property
+    def pending(self) -> int:
+        with self._lock:
+            return len(self._pending)
+
+
+async def wait_for_decision(
+    registry: ApprovalRegistry,
+    request: ApprovalRequest,
+    future: asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision],
+    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
+) -> ApprovalDecision | None:
+    """Await a decision, returning ``None`` when the gate expired or was dropped.
+
+    The gate is always discarded, so an expired id can never be answered later
+    and a cancelled turn leaves nothing behind.
+    """
+    try:
+        return await asyncio.wait_for(future, timeout=timeout)
+    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
+        return None
+    except asyncio.CancelledError:
+        raise
+    finally:
+        registry.discard(request.id)
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "ApprovalDecision",
+    "ApprovalNotFoundError",
+    "ApprovalRegistry",
+    "ApprovalRequest",
+    "DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS",
+    "wait_for_decision",
+]

 def _apply_add_connector(
     arguments: dict[str, Any], service: ConnectorService

     """Register a connector locally and return SSE event dicts for the stream."""
     name = arguments.get("name")

     if preset_id is not None:

         event_data["url"] = url
     return f"registered connector {config.name}", [{"event": "connector", "data": event_data}]

     arguments: dict[str, Any], memory: StudioMemory | None

         return "Memory is not available to this client.", None
 
     kind = str(arguments.get("kind", ""))
     text = str(arguments.get("text", ""))
     data = arguments.get("data")
     try:

     def delete_observation(self, observation_id: str) -> None:

             cursor = self._connection.execute(
                 "DELETE FROM observations WHERE id = ?", (observation_id,)
             )

     def clear_memory(self) -> None:
         with self._lock, self._connection:
             self._connection.execute("DELETE FROM turns")
             self._connection.execute("DELETE FROM observations")
             self._connection.execute("DELETE FROM conversations")
 
     # -- prompt context ----------------------------------------------------
 
     def memory_context(self) -> str:
         """A bounded block of remembered context for the system prompt."""
         observations = self.list_observations(include_dismissed=False)
         confirmed = [item for item in observations if item.status == "confirmed"]
         suggested = [item for item in observations if item.status == "suggested"][
             :MAX_SUGGESTED_IN_CONTEXT
         ]
 
         lines: list[str] = []
         for item in [*confirmed, *suggested]:
             text = item.text[:MAX_CONTEXT_TEXT]
             lines.append(f"- ({item.status}) [{item.kind}] {text}")
 
         if not lines:
             return ""
 
         block = (
             "What you already know about this product manager, from earlier "
             "conversations. Use it naturally; do not recite it back or mention "
             "that you have a memory store. Confirmed items are durable context. "
             "Suggested items are your working guesses and may be wrong.\n" + "\n".join(lines)
         )

         return Turn(

+            message_id=row["message_id"] if "message_id" in keys else None,
+            parent_id=row["parent_id"] if "parent_id" in keys else None,

     @staticmethod
     def _observation_from_row(row: sqlite3.Row) -> Observation:
         try:

         return Observation(

         for line in block.splitlines():

+"""The write-approval gate: it resolves once, expires, and never leaks."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import json
+
+import pytest
+from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.approvals import (
+    ApprovalDecision,
+    ApprovalNotFoundError,
+    ApprovalRegistry,
+    wait_for_decision,
+)
+
+
+def _open(registry: ApprovalRegistry) -> tuple[object, object]:
+    async def _run() -> tuple[object, object]:
+        return registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-1",
+            name="add_job",
+            arguments={"name": "Retention"},
+            prompt="Allow the assistant to add job?",
+        )
+
+    return asyncio.run(_run())
+
+
+def test_open_describes_the_call_for_the_ui() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+    request, _future = _open(registry)
+
+    payload = request.to_dict()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+
+    assert payload["id"].startswith("apv_")
+    assert payload["tool_call_id"] == "call-1"
+    assert payload["name"] == "add_job"
+    assert payload["arguments"] == {"name": "Retention"}
+    assert payload["prompt"] == "Allow the assistant to add job?"
+    assert registry.pending == 1
+
+
+def test_resolve_answers_the_waiting_turn() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+
+    async def _run() -> ApprovalDecision:
+        request, future = registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-1", name="add_job", arguments={}, prompt="?"
+        )
+        pending = asyncio.create_task(wait_for_decision(registry, request, future, timeout=5))
+        await asyncio.sleep(0)
+        registry.resolve(request.id, ApprovalDecision(approved=True, reason="ok"))
+        decision = await pending
+        assert decision is not None
+        return decision
+
+    decision = asyncio.run(_run())
+
+    assert decision.approved is True
+    assert decision.reason == "ok"
+    assert registry.pending == 0
+
+
+def test_an_expired_gate_returns_none_and_is_forgotten() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+
+    async def _run() -> ApprovalDecision | None:
+        request, future = registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-1", name="add_job", arguments={}, prompt="?"
+        )
+        return await wait_for_decision(registry, request, future, timeout=0.01)
+
+    assert asyncio.run(_run()) is None
+    assert registry.pending == 0
+
+
+def test_a_gate_answers_only_once() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+
+    async def _run() -> None:
+        request, future = registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-1", name="add_job", arguments={}, prompt="?"
+        )
+        registry.resolve(request.id, ApprovalDecision(approved=True))
+        with pytest.raises(ApprovalNotFoundError):
+            registry.resolve(request.id, ApprovalDecision(approved=False))
+        await asyncio.sleep(0)
+        assert future.done()
+
+    asyncio.run(_run())
+
+
+def test_an_unknown_gate_cannot_be_resolved() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+
+    with pytest.raises(ApprovalNotFoundError):
+        registry.resolve("apv_missing", ApprovalDecision(approved=True))
+
+
+def test_cancel_all_drops_every_pending_gate() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+
+    async def _run() -> list[bool]:
+        _first, first_future = registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-1", name="add_job", arguments={}, prompt="?"
+        )
+        _second, second_future = registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-2", name="delete_job", arguments={}, prompt="?"
+        )
+        registry.cancel_all()
+        await asyncio.sleep(0)
+        return [first_future.cancelled(), second_future.cancelled()]
+
+    assert asyncio.run(_run()) == [True, True]
+    assert registry.pending == 0
+
+
+def test_the_decision_serializes_for_the_stream() -> None:
+    decision = ApprovalDecision(approved=False, reason="not this time")
+
+    assert json.loads(json.dumps(decision.__dict__)) == {
+        "approved": False,
+        "reason": "not this time",
+    }

+    tool_result: str = "ok"
+
+    def __init__(self, url: str) -> None:
+        self.url = url
+
+    async def __aenter__(self) -> _Mcp:
+        return self
+
+    async def __aexit__(self, *exc: Any) -> bool:
+        return False
+
+    async def list_tools(self) -> list[Any]:
+        return [
+            SimpleNamespace(
+                name="add_job",
+                description="Create a job",
+                input_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}}},
+            ),
+            SimpleNamespace(
+                name="get_jobs",
+                description="List jobs",
+                input_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {}},
+            ),
+        ]
+
+    async def call_tool(self, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+        _Mcp.calls.append((name, arguments))
+        return _Mcp.tool_result
+
+
+def _chunk(
+    content: str | None = None,
+    tool_calls: list[Any] | None = None,
+    reasoning: str | None = None,
+) -> Any:
+    delta = SimpleNamespace(
+        content=content,
+        tool_calls=tool_calls,
+        reasoning_content=reasoning,
+    )
+    return SimpleNamespace(choices=[SimpleNamespace(delta=delta)])
+
+
+def _tool_call(arguments: str, name: str = "get_jobs") -> Any:
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        index=0,
+        id="call-1",
+        function=SimpleNamespace(name=name, arguments=arguments),
+    )
+
+
+def _install(monkeypatch, streams: list[_FakeStream]) -> None:
+    async def _healthy(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> tuple[bool, str]:
+        return True, "ok"
+
+    _Mcp.calls = []
+    _Mcp.tool_result = "ok"
+    monkeypatch.setattr(chat, "check_llm_health", _healthy)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(chat, "McpClient", _Mcp)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(chat, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(chat, "AsyncOpenAI", lambda **kwargs: _FakeOpenAI(streams, **kwargs))
+
+
+def _parse(frames: list[str]) -> list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]]:
+    events: list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] = []
+    for frame in frames:
+        name = None
+        data = None
+        for line in frame.splitlines():
+            if line.startswith("event: "):
+                name = line[len("event: ") :]
+            elif line.startswith("data: "):
+                data = line[len("data: ") :]
+        if name and data is not None:
+            events.append((name, json.loads(data)))
+    return events
+
+
+def _collect(request: ChatRequest, approvals: ApprovalRegistry | None = None) -> list[str]:
+    async def _run() -> list[str]:
+        return [frame async for frame in chat.stream_chat(request, approvals=approvals)]
+
+    return asyncio.run(_run())
+
+
+def _collect_answering(
+    request: ChatRequest,
+    approvals: ApprovalRegistry,
+    decision: ApprovalDecision,
+) -> list[str]:
+    """Consume the turn, answering the first approval gate that appears."""
+
+    async def _run() -> list[str]:
+        frames: list[str] = []
+        async for frame in chat.stream_chat(request, approvals=approvals):
+            frames.append(frame)
+            if frame.startswith("event: approval"):
+                payload = json.loads(frame.split("data: ", 1)[1])
+                approvals.resolve(payload["id"], decision)
+        return frames
+
+    return asyncio.run(_run())
+
+

+        ("m-1", None),

+    connection.executescript(
+        """
+        CREATE TABLE conversations (
+            id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
+            created_at TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
+        );
+        CREATE TABLE turns (
+            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,

+            content TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL

+        INSERT INTO conversations VALUES ('c1', 'Old', 'now', 'now');
+        INSERT INTO turns (conversation_id, role, content, created_at)
+            VALUES ('c1', 'user', 'hello', 'now');
+        INSERT INTO turns (conversation_id, role, content, created_at)
+            VALUES ('c1', 'assistant', 'hi', 'now');
+        """
+    )
+    connection.commit()
+    connection.close()

 # Repository Architecture
 
 Agentic ODI is a uv workspace with a single root `pyproject.toml` for shared tooling. Python distributions are imported by their stable `agentic_odi_*` package names; directory layout does not leak into imports.
 
 ## Layout
 
 ```text
 apps/
   cli/            agentic_odi_cli         Typer CLI: local SQLite or remote MCP
   mcp-server/     agentic_odi_mcp_server  FastMCP server over HTTP
   studio-api/     agentic_odi_studio_api  FastAPI sidecar for the Studio SPA
   studio/         React + TypeScript + Vite SPA and Tauri 2 shell
 packages/
   core/           agentic_odi_core        Domain, services, repositories, contract
   connectors/     agentic_odi_connectors  MCP client connectors and catalog
 infra/cloudflare/ Worker script; wrangler.jsonc lives at the repo root
 scripts/          Dev launcher, binary build, installer checks
 tests/            Cross-package contract and launcher tests only
 docs/             Architecture, reference material, Superpowers artifacts
 packaging/        PyInstaller spec for the CLI binary
 ```
 
 ## Dependency Direction
 
 ```text
 apps/cli ──────────────┐
 apps/mcp-server ───────┼──▶ packages/core
 apps/studio-api ───────┘         ▲
                                  │
 apps/cli ──────────────▶ packages/connectors
 ```
 
 - `packages/core` depends on no other workspace package.
 - `packages/connectors` depends on `core` only where it needs shared models.
 - Every runnable app may depend on `core`; none of them imports another app.
 - The React SPA only talks to `apps/studio-api` over `/api`; it never calls MCP or the LLM directly.
+- The SPA's conversation runtime is assistant-ui, bound to the Studio's own
+  store in `apps/studio/src/assistant/`. That directory
+  is the whole bridge: `convert.ts` maps the two message models in both
+  directions, `StudioRuntime.tsx` wires the runtime callbacks, and
+  `attachments.ts` extracts files in the browser. The library is presentation
+  only — it holds no product state and makes no network calls of its own.
 
 ## Persistence
 
 - `SQLiteRepository` is the production default for the CLI, MCP server, and Studio API.
 - The default database is `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_DB`.
 - Studio conversation history and PM memory use a separate SQLite database,
   `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`. They are
   sidecar-local and never enter the ODI repository or the MCP contract.
 - `build_repository()` chooses SQLite by default and `InMemoryRepository` when `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:`, which is what tests use.
 - The CLI selects its backend with `--backend local|mcp` or `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND`.
 - The Studio API selects `local` (direct service calls) or `mcp` (passthrough) with `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` or `create_app(backend=...)`.
 
 ## MCP Contract
 
 `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` owns `ToolName`, `ToolSpec`, `TOOL_SPECS`, and `TOOL_NAMES`. The live FastMCP registry is asserted against it by `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py`; the CLI's local handlers are checked by `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py`.
 
 ## Entry Points
 
 | Command | Module |
 |---|---|
 | `agentic-odi` | `agentic_odi_cli.cli:app` |
 | `agentic-odi-server` / `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | `agentic_odi_mcp_server.mcp_server:main` |
 | `agentic-odi-studio-api` | `agentic_odi_studio_api.main:main` |
 | `uv run python scripts/dev.py` | Dev launcher (MCP + Studio API) |
 
 ## Related
 
 - [Data flow](data-flow.md)
 - [Testing](testing.md)

 # Data Flow
 
 ## Sources of Truth
 
 | Layer | Owns | Persists |
 |---|---|---|
 | `packages/core` | `Job`, `Step`, `Outcome`, `CustomerOutcome`, `ODIService`, repository protocol | SQLite event log + snapshots |
 | `apps/mcp-server` | MCP tool adapters over `ODIService` | `build_repository()` selects SQLite in production and in-memory for `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` |
 | `apps/studio-api` | Studio API, canvas projection, chat tool loop, conversation history, PM memory | Via the same repository when the local backend is active; conversations and memory in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` |
-| `apps/studio` | Presentation state, optimistic canvas updates | Browser cache only |
+| `apps/studio` | Presentation state, the visible conversation path, optimistic canvas updates; the conversation runtime is assistant-ui | Browser cache only |
 | `apps/cli` | Terminal rendering, local/remote backend selection | SQLite directly for `local`, no local writes for `mcp` |
 
 ## Write Paths
 
 ### Local CLI
 
 ```text
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes add
   -> LocalBackend
   -> ODIService
   -> SQLiteRepository
   -> IntentStore (append) + snapshot refresh
 ```
 
 ### MCP
 
 ```text
 MCP client / Studio MCP mode / CLI --backend mcp
   -> FastMCP tool
   -> ODIService
   -> configured Repository
 ```
 
 `apps/mcp-server` builds its repository once at import time with `build_repository()`. Production uses SQLite; tests set `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` (the root test suite does this in `tests/conftest.py`).
 
 ### Studio API
 
 ```text
 apps/studio SPA
   -> /api/canvas, /api/steps, /api/outcomes
   -> backend=local: ODIService -> Repository
   -> backend=mcp:   call_mcp_tool -> MCP server -> ODIService -> Repository
 
 apps/studio SPA
   -> /api/chat
   -> stream_chat -> OpenAI-compatible LLM -> MCP tool calls
   -> StudioMemory (conversation turns + remembered observations)
+
+apps/studio SPA
+  -> POST /api/approvals/{id}
+  -> ApprovalRegistry -> resolves the paused turn's pending gate
 ```
 
 The studio memory is a separate SQLite file, not an ODI repository. It never
 feeds the canvas; it only supplies bounded context to the next chat turn.
 
 The SPA sends `mcp_url` with every data request for compatibility. In `local` mode the sidecar ignores it; in `mcp` mode it is required for canvas and mutations.
 
+## The Conversation
+
+One turn is one SSE stream, and the SPA renders it as typed parts rather than a
+string. Events, in the order they can appear:
+
+| Event | Payload | Meaning |
+|---|---|---|
+| `status` | `phase` | `health_check`, `mcp_tools`, `model`, or `offline` |
+| `conversation` | `id`, `title` | The thread this turn belongs to |
+| `reasoning` | `text` | Model thinking, rendered in a disclosure, never persisted as prose |
+| `delta` | `text` | Prose appended to the open text part |
+| `tool` | `name`, `status`, `preview` | `start`, `ok`, `error`, or `declined` |
+| `approval` | `id`, `tool_call_id`, `name`, `arguments`, `prompt` | A write is waiting for the person |
+| `source` | `id`, `title`, `filename`, `mediaType`, `preview` | What the turn actually read |
+| `ui` | `id`, `spec` | A validated generated surface |
+| `memory`, `connector`, `canvas_dirty` | — | Side effects the SPA applies without a refresh |
+| `message` / `error` | `content` / `StudioError` | Exactly one terminal event |
+
+Approval gates are process-local and single-user. `ApprovalRegistry` holds one
+`asyncio` future per pending write; `POST /api/approvals/{id}` resolves it and
+the same stream continues with the call or with a declined tool result. A
+timeout (300 s), a cancelled turn, or sidecar shutdown closes the gate, so a
+turn always terminates.
+
+The SPA owns the visible path; the sidecar owns the record. Turns persist with
+`message_id` and `parent_id`, and the conversation stores `head_id`:
+
+```text
+GET   /api/conversations/latest                -> thread + turns (resume)
+GET   /api/conversations/{id}/tree             -> branch tree + head
+PATCH /api/conversations/{id} {"head_id"}      -> record the visible branch
+```
+
+A conversation written before ids existed has none, so the tree endpoint
+synthesises a linear chain and old threads still open. `apps/studio` never
+invents a branch the sidecar cannot reproduce.
+
 ## Read Paths
 
 ```text
 ODIService.get_jobs / get_job_map / get_outcomes
   -> Repository read-through state
   -> Pydantic models
   -> JSON (CLI --json, MCP text payload, Studio canvas)
 ```
 
 The Studio canvas falls back to the demo seed only in `mcp` mode when MCP is unreachable or returns no jobs. `local` mode returns exactly what is in the local database, including an empty canvas.
 
 ## Configuration
 
 | Variable | Used by | Default |
 |---|---|---|
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | core SQLite repository | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | CLI, Studio API | `local` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | CLI, Studio defaults | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB` | Studio API memory | `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DIST` | Studio API, dev launcher | `apps/studio/dist` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT` | Tauri shell | auto-detected |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `http://localhost:8001/v1` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local-tools-model` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local` |
 
 ## Trust Boundaries
 
 - The SPA runs in a browser or Tauri webview and only trusts the sidecar origin.
 - The sidecar may reach MCP and the LLM; CORS is restricted to known Studio origins.
 - MCP is an HTTP service with no authentication in local development. Do not expose it directly to the internet; the Cloudflare setup tunnels the sidecar, not MCP.
 
 ## The Failure Path
 
 A failure is a first-class result, not an empty success. The path is the same
 for the CLI, the sidecar, and the SPA.
 
 ```text
 MCP tool result (text)
   -> agentic_odi_core.remote.parse_tool_result
   -> StudioError { code, message, detail, suggestion, retryable, request_id }
   -> sidecar: StudioHTTPError -> HTTP status + {"error": StudioError}
   -> SPA: StudioApiError -> FailurePanel (message, detail, suggestion, Retry)
 ```
 
 - **One error body.** Every HTTP failure is `{"error": StudioError}`. The SPA
   also reads a legacy `{"detail": "..."}` body, so an older sidecar still
   produces a readable message. Write routes no longer wrap their result in
   `{"ok": true, "result": ...}`: a success is the object, a delete is
   `{"deleted": id}`.
 - **One terminal chat event.** Every `/api/chat` stream ends with exactly one
   `message` or one `error`. A recoverable tool error stays a tool result the
   model can read, but it is reported as `status: "error"` and counted. A fatal
   failure ends the stream with `event: error` carrying the `StudioError`.
 - **Request ids.** The sidecar accepts or mints `X-Request-ID`, echoes it on
   the response, and puts it on every SSE frame. The MCP server's own log line
   and the `Execution` record (#82) do not carry it yet, and authentication
   (#90) is out of scope.
 - **The canvas is a union.** `CanvasState` is `loading | ready | empty |
   error`. An empty canvas is an invitation; a failed canvas is a failure panel
   with Retry. The two never look the same.
 - **The turn log is safe.** One JSON line per turn carries the request id, the
   model, the round and tool counts, the error count, the duration, and the
   outcome. Sensitive keys are dropped rather than redacted, so no token, key,
   or customer quote can reach the log.

 # Testing
 
 ## Commands
 
 ```bash
 uv run pytest                       # all packages + root contract/launcher tests
 uv run pytest packages/core         # one package
 uv run pytest tests/contract        # MCP contract only
-uv run mypy apps packages tests
+uv run mypy apps brand packages
 uv run ruff check .
 uv run ruff format --check .
 uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages
+uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r website/
 ```
 
 The root `pyproject.toml` owns pytest, coverage, ruff, mypy, and bandit configuration. There is no per-package test configuration to keep in sync.
 
 ## Layout
 
-Tests live next to their package (`packages/*/tests`, `apps/*/tests`). Root `tests/` contains only cross-package checks:
+Tests live next to their package (`packages/*/tests`, `apps/*/tests`). `testpaths` in the root `pyproject.toml` covers `apps`, `brand`, `packages`, `tests`, and `website`, so one `uv run pytest` collects all of them.
 
+### `packages/core/tests/`
+
+- `test_models.py` — domain models and their validation rules.
+- `test_service.py` — `ODIService` CRUD, Opportunity Score, and thesis rendering.
+- `test_repository.py` — `InMemoryRepository` behavior.
+- `test_sqlite_repository.py` — SQLite persistence and round-trips.
+- `test_repository_factory.py` — `build_repository()` variant selection.
+- `test_schema.py` — schema creation and migration.
+- `test_events.py` — event-store schema and legacy-database backfill.
+- `test_intent_store.py` — append-only Intent Store ordering.
+- `test_pagination.py` — list pagination across both repositories and the service.
+- `test_errors.py` — the ODI error hierarchy and its messages.
+- `test_evidence_not_found.py` — actionable evidence-not-found errors.
+- `test_consent_pause.py` — acting tools wait for PM consent.
+- `test_remote.py` — shared MCP tool-result and error parser.

 **The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation:
 an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact
 Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent
 connected to the MCP server.
 
 The Studio runs three ways locally, plus a hosted deployment. All of them serve
 the same SPA, which talks only to the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the
 SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM directly.

 ```text
 ┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
 │  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  apps/studio-api (sidecar)    │
 │  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
 │  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
 └────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
                                              │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
                                              │  - conversations + PM memory  │
                                              └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                              │ MCP (HTTP)
                                                              ▼
                                              ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                              │  apps/mcp-server :8000/mcp    │
                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
                                                              ▲
                                                              │ OpenAI-compatible
                                              ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                                              │  Your local LLM backend       │
                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
 ```

 ### Slash commands
 
 Type `/` to open the palette. `Up`/`Down` move, `Enter` or `Tab` runs the
 selected command, `Esc` closes it. Commands are handled in the SPA and never call
 the model, so they work when it is offline.
 
 | Command | Effect |
 |---|---|
 | `/help` | Every command, as a notice in the transcript |
 | `/start` | Resume the context conversation |

 | `/home` | Return to the empty stage |
 | `/jobs` | Job summary, then the job map |
 | `/landscape`, `/jobmap`, `/evidence`, `/settings` | Open that lens beside the conversation |
 | `/impact`, `/capture` | Start the conversation that produces the card. `/capture` falls back to the offline form when no model answers. |

 ### The welcome tour
 
 The tour is the front door, the context conversation is the first room. It is
 skippable at every step (`Skip the tour` or `Escape`), resumable (progress is
 stored after every transition in `localStorage["studio.onboarding"]`), and
 replayable from Settings.
 
 Everything lives in `apps/studio/src/onboarding/`:
 
 | File | Role |
 |---|---|
 | `content.ts` | Steps and goal copy as typed data — the only place the words live |
 | `machine.ts` | Pure state transitions, no React or storage |
 | `storage.ts` | Versioned, defensive `localStorage` persistence |
 | `OnboardingProvider.tsx` | Auto-open, persistence, replay |
 | `FirstRunWizard.tsx`, `steps.tsx`, `onboarding.css` | The dialog |
 | `../features/flags.ts` | The `firstRunWizard` toggle |
 
 `App.tsx` only wires the provider and the wizard around the existing shell;
 the chat, canvas, and sidecar code are untouched.
 
 #### Toggling the tour
 
 `firstRunWizard` defaults to on. Resolution order, highest first:
 
 | Source | Example | Use |
 |---|---|---|
 | Query parameter | `?flags=firstRunWizard:off` | QA a build without rebuilding |
 | Local override | `localStorage["studio.flags.firstRunWizard"] = "off"` | Per-browser opt-out |
 | Build environment | `VITE_STUDIO_FIRST_RUN_WIZARD=off npm --prefix apps/studio run build` | Ship it dark |
 | Default | on | |
 
 Accepted values are `1`/`0`, `true`/`false`, `on`/`off`, `yes`/`no`, and
 `enabled`/`disabled`. With the flag off, no dialog renders, no onboarding state
 is written, and Settings hides the replay action.
 
 ### Guidance, not gates
 
 The setup conversation is a nudge, never a prerequisite. If you skip it, the
 home stage keeps a dashed **Tell me what you're building** pill; it reopens the
 conversation exactly where you left off. `/start` and Settings do the same. The conversation also understands a
 natural reply: say "skip", "not now", or "show me the landscape" and it reacts
 instead of recording it as an answer. When a brief exists, it opens on a review
 and asks what changed rather than asking everything again.
 
 ### Without a model
 
 When the LLM is unreachable the Studio keeps working:
 
 - A **Working by hand** strip explains the state and offers capture, job map,
   and context.
 - Messages still return deterministic ODI guidance from the sidecar, labelled
   **Local guidance**.
 - Jobs can be created, renamed, and deleted; steps added, edited, and removed;
   outcomes recorded, re-scored, and removed. All of it goes through the same
   local repository the model uses.
 - Settings → Base URL and Model reconnect the assistant whenever you are ready.
 
 The user's context is sent with every chat request, so the assistant starts from
 the product, audience, job, and problem rather than asking for them again.
 
 ### The thread is the room
 
 Capture, scoring, simulation, and decisions are conversations. The storefront
 never asks the PM to leave the thread to do work: the agent asks for the
 customer's words or the bet in plain language, then renders the surface that
 carries it. A lens exists for reading and for people who prefer a click, not for
 doing the work.
 
 That is also enforced in the agent's system prompt: it is told to keep every
 artifact in the conversation, never to send the PM to a panel, and to end each
 reply with the next move as an action on the surface.
 
+### The conversation runtime
+
+The transcript is not a hand-rolled message list. It runs on **assistant-ui**,
+a React runtime for streaming assistants, bound to the Studio's own store with
+`useExternalStoreRuntime`, so the thread gains real conversation capabilities
+without giving up the message model the sidecar already understands.
+
+| Capability | What it means here |
+|---|---|
+| **Streaming** | `delta` frames append to the open prose part; the send button becomes stop. |
+| **Reasoning** | `reasoning` frames render in a collapsed *Thought for a moment* disclosure. Never persisted, never counted as the answer. |
+| **Tools** | Each MCP call is a trace chip with its status and a short preview of what came back. |
+| **Approval** | A writing tool (`add_`, `create_`, `update_`, `delete_`, `ingest_`, `remove_`) pauses the turn until you answer **Allow** or **Decline**. A decline is a tool result, not an error: the model is told no and may propose something else. |
+| **Sources** | Every tool call that returned data emits a `source`, titled with the tool and a preview. Provenance is what the turn actually read; a citation is never invented. |
+| **Attachments** | Text-like files (`.md`, `.mdx`, `.json`, `.csv`, `.yaml`, `.log`, `text/*`) and images (PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF, at most 5 MB). Text is extracted in the browser, capped at 20k characters, and sent with the turn. Nothing is stored server-side. |
+| **Branching** | **Edit** a user turn or **Regenerate** a reply and both versions are kept as siblings. `‹ 2 of 3 ›` steps between them, and the visible branch is saved as the conversation's `head_id`, so a reload reopens the branch you were reading. |
+| **Suggestions** | The empty-stage pills are chosen from the canvas and handed to the runtime as suggestion prompts. |
+| **Generative UI** | A validated `UiNode` travels as an assistant-ui **data part** (`data-odi-surface`) and renders through the same `UiRenderer`. The catalog stays ours and server-validated. |
+| **Voice** | Deliberately not wired yet. The seam is `adapters.dictation` plus `ComposerPrimitive.Dictate`: no backend change and no message-model change. It waits because Tauri's WebKit webview support for the Web Speech API is uneven, and a microphone button that works in only one shell is worse than none. |
+
+#### Where the bridge lives
+
+| File | Role |
+|---|---|
+| `apps/studio/src/assistant/convert.ts` | The only mapping between `ChatMessage`/`ChatPart` and assistant-ui parts, in both directions. Pure, and tested without a runtime. |
+| `apps/studio/src/assistant/StudioRuntime.tsx` | `useExternalStoreRuntime`: `onNew`, `onEdit`, `onReload`, `onCancel`, `setMessages`, `onRespondToToolApproval`, suggestions, attachments. |
+| `apps/studio/src/assistant/attachments.ts` | The attachment adapter and the browser-side text/image extraction. |
+| `apps/studio/src/assistant/parts.tsx` | One renderer per part: text, reasoning, tool (with its approval), source, file, generated surface. |
+| `apps/studio/src/components/chat/Conversation.tsx` | `MessagePrimitive.Parts`, the branch picker, the action bar, and the in-place edit composer. |
+| `apps/studio/src/components/chat/ThreadComposer.tsx` | `ComposerPrimitive` plus the slash palette and connector chips. |
+
+The sidecar remains the source of truth for what happened. Its additions are
+opt-in and additive: `reasoning`, `source`, and `approval` stream events;
+`attachments` and `approvals` on `/api/chat`; `GET
+/api/conversations/{id}/tree`; and `PATCH /api/conversations/{id}`. A client that
+sends neither flag sees exactly the stream it saw before, which is what the CLI
+and older clients do.
+
+The approval gate is per-process and single-user by design. `ApprovalRegistry`
+waits on an `asyncio` future, `POST /api/approvals/{id}` answers it, and a
+timeout (300 s) or a cancelled turn resolves as a declined write, so a turn can
+never hang and a double click can never run a tool twice. That is the right size
+for a loopback sidecar with one person at the keyboard; it is not a durable job
+queue, and it is not pretending to be one.
+
+#### Extending the conversation
+
+A new kind of part is added in exactly two places — the mapping in `convert.ts`
+and the component in `parts.tsx` — and then registered in the `components` map
+in `Conversation.tsx`. Do not add a second message list, and never let an unknown
+part reach the screen as JSON: the converter drops what it does not understand on
+purpose, and `convert.test.ts` holds that line.
+
 ### What it remembers
 
 The studio keeps a small, local, editable model of the person it is helping. It
 is not a profile and not a transcript index; it is the handful of things that
 change the next answer.
 
 | Kind | What it captures |
 |---|---|
 | `career` | The PM's role, remit, and what success looks like for them |
 | `opportunity` | The opportunity or bet currently in play |
 | `business` | Goals, metrics, and commercial constraints |
 | `stakeholder` | Who else matters and what they care about |
 | `constraint` | Time, budget, policy, or technical limits |
 | `evidence` | What has actually been heard or measured |
 | `preference` | How the PM likes to work and be spoken to |
 
 Each note is `suggested` or `confirmed`. Suggested notes appear first under
 **What I know** with **Yes, that's right**, **That's not it**, and **Edit**;
 confirmed notes can be edited or forgotten. The PM can also add a note by hand.
 Nothing is silently promoted: the agent may propose, but the person decides.
 
 The agent writes notes through a `remember` tool during a normal reply. The
 sidecar applies it, emits a `memory` SSE event, and the panel updates without a
 refresh. Memory writes are best-effort — a database failure never turns a good
 answer into an error.
 
 Storage is a separate SQLite file from the ODI repository:
 `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`
 (`:memory:` is supported and is what the tests use). The API is small:
 
 | Method | Path | Purpose |
 |---|---|---|
 | `GET` | `/api/memory/observations` | Everything the agent believes |
 | `POST` | `/api/memory/observations` | Add a note by hand |
 | `PATCH` | `/api/memory/observations/{id}` | Edit text, confidence, or status |
 | `DELETE` | `/api/memory/observations/{id}` | Forget one note |
 | `DELETE` | `/api/memory` | Forget all notes and conversations |
 
 **Forget everything** is a two-step confirmation and also clears the visible
 thread, because the server deletes the conversations behind it.
 
 ### The thread comes back
 
 Conversations are stored beside the memory. On launch the SPA asks
 `GET /api/conversations/latest`, restores that thread's user and assistant
 turns, and continues with the same `conversation_id` on the next message. **New
 conversation** starts a fresh one without touching the memory; **Forget
 everything** removes both. The composer stays usable while the restore is in
 flight, and a restore failure simply leaves the room empty.
 
 ## Rich responses
 
 The copilot does not only talk. When a surface carries the evidence better than a
 paragraph, the agent renders one **inline in the conversation**: a scored
 outcome, a ranked opportunity board, a before/after simulation of a bet, a
 customer quote with its lineage, the eight-stage job map, an opportunity thesis, or a decision record.
 Three properties keep this safe and cheap to extend:
 
 - **The catalog is closed and owned by the SPA.**
   `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` declares nine primitives and seven cards, their
   JSON Schema props, and the description the model reads. There is no HTML, no
   eval, and no third-party component in the path. Prose is rendered by the same
   `Markdown` component the transcript already used.
 - **The sidecar is catalog-agnostic.** The SPA sends the catalog with each turn;
   the sidecar derives the `render_ui` tool schema from it, validates what comes
   back, and streams a `ui` SSE event. Invalid props return to the model as a tool
   result naming the exact violation, and the loop offers the tool again, so a
   fumbled prop is corrected in the same reply. A client that sends no catalog
   never sees the tool.
 - **Cards are views, never actors.** Every button is an `intent` string that the
   agent receives as the user's next message — one authority, one audit trail.
 
 A surface is one node tree, streamed as one event:
 
 ```json
 {
   "type": "outcome-card",
   "props": {
     "id": "O-1",
     "statement": "Minimize the time it takes to propagate secrets across environments",
     "importance": 9,
     "satisfaction": 3
   }
 }
 ```
 
 The opportunity thesis is the intent-first card: one opportunity with its
 importance, satisfaction, the gap in plain words, the thesis itself, and the
 smallest next move. It is the shape the agent reaches for when the PM is deciding
 what to chase, rather than when they are inspecting a single score.
 
 The conversation keeps the order the agent produced: a `delta` appends to the
 open prose part, a `ui` event opens a card, and the next `delta` opens a new
 paragraph after it. The opportunity score is computed from importance and
 satisfaction when the agent omits it, so the ODI formula has exactly one home
 (`src/lib/odi.ts`). Unknown component types degrade to a quiet fallback; a tree
 that fails validation is dropped whole, and the surrounding prose still reads.
 
 ### Adding a surface
 
 1. Add an entry to `CATALOG` in `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` — props as a
    JSON Schema subset, plus the description the model will read.
 2. Register the component in `apps/studio/src/ui/registry.ts`.
 3. Implement it in `apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx` (domain shape) or
    `apps/studio/src/ui/primitives.tsx` (composition).
 4. Run `npm --prefix apps/studio test`. The `registry parity` test fails if the
    catalog and the registry drift apart.
 
 No server change is needed, and no new dependency.
 
 ## Hosted (experimental)
 
 The built SPA is also served from Cloudflare Workers at
 **[https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**.
 The UI loads without a backend; canvas data, chat, and mutations need the local
 sidecar and MCP server. Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers
 Builds. See [Deployment](deployment.md) for the Worker setup.

 ## Desktop signing & updater secrets
 
 Self-updating and code signing are **env-driven**: if a secret is absent, an
 unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub
 Actions secrets.
 
 | Secret | Purpose |
 |---|---|
 | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | Signs updater artifacts (`.sig`) and the `latest.json` manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate`. |
 | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password for the private key (optional when the key has none). |
 | `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` / `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 `.p12`) and its password. |
 | `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | macOS signing identity. |
 | `APPLE_ID` / `APPLE_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | macOS notarization credentials. |
 | `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` / `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config. |
 
 Releases are published by `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml` when a `v*` tag
 is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via
 **Settings → Check for updates**.
 
 ### Managing the updater signing key
 
 The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can
 verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The **public** key is
 embedded in `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`plugins.updater.pubkey`) and is
 safe to commit. The **private** key must never be committed, logged, printed in
 CI, or attached to a build artifact.
 
 1. **Generate a key pair** (only if you need a new one). Leave `-p ""` for a
    passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it:
 
    ```bash
    npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f
    ```
 
    This writes `living-studio.key` (private, `0600`) and `living-studio.key.pub`
    (public).
 
 2. **Paste the public key** into `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`:
 
    ```jsonc
    {
      "plugins": {
        "updater": {
          "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"],
          "pubkey": "<contents of living-studio.key.pub>"
        }
      }
    }
    ```
 
 3. **Store the private key outside the repository** (the repo root is
    git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions:
 
    ```bash
    mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys
    mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/
    chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
    ```
 
    Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/
    Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives.
    Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing
    installs.
 
 4. **Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret** (Settings → Secrets and
    variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI:
 
    ```bash
    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body ""   # only if you set a password
    ```
 
 5. **Verify** the secrets exist (values are never displayed):
 
    ```bash
    gh secret list
    ```
 
 6. **Rotate** by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the
    new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into
    their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public
    key ahead of the cut-over.
 
 > [!CAUTION]
 > If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new
 > pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release.
 
 ## Connecting an LLM
 
 The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM backend with tool-calling support to
 drive the agent. For a fully local setup, see
 [Local LLM Backend](local-llm.md).
 
 ## Agent-Driven Testing
 
 Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it starts
 both processes, opens the browser, sends a test message, and reports the results.
 
 Type `/test` to have the agent run all tests and report the results
 automatically.

+def validate_connector_config(config: dict) -> dict:
+    """Validate a connector preset config dict.
+
+    Checks that required keys are present, kind is a registered kind,
+    health_url is an HTTP(S) URL, and ingest_endpoint is non-empty.
+    Returns the config unchanged on success; raises ConfigurationError
+    with the list of bad keys on failure.
+    """
+    bad: list[str] = []
+    for key in REQUIRED_KEYS:
+        if key not in config or config[key] in (None, ""):
+            bad.append(key)
+    if "kind" in config and config["kind"] not in KNOWN_KINDS:
+        bad.append("kind")
+    if (
+        "health_url" in config
+        and config["health_url"] not in (None, "")
+        and not config["health_url"].startswith(("http://", "https://"))
+    ):
+        bad.append("health_url")
+    if bad:
+        raise ConfigurationError(bad)
+    return config
+
+
+def _load_and_validate_presets() -> None:
+    """Read connectors.json and validate every preset at import time.
+
+    Exits the process with code 1 if any preset is invalid.
+    """
+    path = config_path()
+    if not path.exists():
+        return
+    try:
+        with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            payload = json.load(handle)
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
+        print(f"Error reading connectors config: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        sys.exit(1)
+    presets = payload.get("connectors", [])
+    if not isinstance(presets, list):
+        print("Error: connectors config must contain a 'connectors' list", file=sys.stderr)
+        sys.exit(1)
+    bad_presets = []
+    for preset in presets:
+        try:
+            validate_connector_config(preset)
+        except ConfigurationError as exc:
+            bad_presets.append((preset, exc.keys))
+    if bad_presets:

+            print(

             source_name=self.name,
             source_kind=self.kind,

     async def ingest(self) -> IngestBatch:
         batch = IngestBatch(connector_name=self.name)
         try:
             status, body = self._request()
         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
             batch.errors.append(str(exc))
             return batch
         if not 200 <= status < 400:
             batch.errors.append(f"HTTP {status} from {self.settings.url}")
             return batch
         text = body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
         try:
             payload: Any = json.loads(text)
         except json.JSONDecodeError:
             payload = text
         records = self._items(payload)
         for index, item in enumerate(records):
             batch.records.append(self._record(item, index))
         return batch

 def evaluate_outcome_statement(statement: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
     """Return format feedback for a desired-outcome statement."""
     text = statement.strip()
     lowered = text.lower()
     padded = f" {lowered} "
     issues: list[str] = []
     suggestions: list[str] = []
 
     direction: str | None = None
     if lowered.startswith("minimize"):
         direction = "minimize"
     elif lowered.startswith("maximize"):
         direction = "maximize"
     else:
         issues.append("Statement must start with 'Minimize' or 'Maximize'.")
         suggestions.append("Start with 'Minimize/Maximize the [metric] ...'.")
 
     if " the " not in padded:
         issues.append("Name the object of control after 'the'.")
         suggestions.append("Say what is being minimized or maximized, e.g. 'the time to ...'.")
 
     if not any(marker in padded for marker in _CONTEXT_MARKERS):
         issues.append("Add the execution context with 'when ...', 'while ...', or 'before ...'.")
         suggestions.append("Close with the situation, e.g. '... when onboarding a new customer'.")
 
     if len(text.split()) < 4:
         issues.append("Statement is too short to describe a measurable outcome.")
         suggestions.append("Describe the metric, the object, and the context.")
 
     if len(text) > 200:
         issues.append("Statement is longer than 200 characters; keep it to one measurable outcome.")
         suggestions.append("Split broad statements into separate outcomes.")
 
     vague = [term for term in _VAGUE_TERMS if term in lowered]
     if vague:
         issues.append(f"Replace vague terms with a measurable metric: {', '.join(vague)}.")
         suggestions.append("Use a metric such as time, cost, effort, errors, or likelihood.")
 
     return {
         "statement": text,
         "valid": not issues,
         "direction": direction,
         "issues": issues,
         "suggestions": suggestions,
     }

 from typing import Any
 
 from agentic_odi_core.errors import ConflictError, StoreError
 from agentic_odi_core.events import (
     DEFAULT_DEVICE,
     DEFAULT_WORKSPACE,
     Event,
     new_event_id,
 )
 
 _COLUMNS = {
     "event_id": "TEXT",
     "workspace_id": "TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'local'",
     "device_id": "TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'local'",
     "server_seq": "INTEGER",
 }
 
 
 class IntentStore:
     """SQLite implementation of the append-only event contract."""
 
     def __init__(self, db_path: str = "intent_store.db", check_same_thread: bool = True) -> None:
         self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, check_same_thread=check_same_thread)
+        # WAL lets readers and one writer work at once; the busy timeout makes
+        # a second writer wait for the lock (the CLI, the sidecar, and a test
+        # can all hold a connection to the same file) instead of raising
+        # "database is locked" the moment the lock is taken.
         self.conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;")
+        self.conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000;")
         self._init_db()
 
     def _init_db(self) -> None:
         with self.conn:
             self.conn.execute(
                 """
                 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
                     id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                     event_id TEXT,
                     workspace_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'local',
                     device_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'local',
                     timestamp TEXT NOT NULL,
                     event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
                     payload TEXT NOT NULL,
                     server_seq INTEGER
                 )
                 """
             )
             self._migrate_events_table()
             self.conn.execute(
                 "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS events_event_id ON events(event_id)"
             )
             self.conn.execute(
                 """
                 CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS events_workspace_server
                 ON events(workspace_id, server_seq)
                 """
             )
             self.conn.execute(
                 """
                 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sync_state (
                     workspace_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                     remote_url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
                     last_server_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
                     updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
                 )
                 """
             )
 
     def _migrate_events_table(self) -> None:
         existing = {row[1] for row in self.conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(events)").fetchall()}
         for column, definition in _COLUMNS.items():
             if column not in existing:
                 self.conn.execute(f"ALTER TABLE events ADD COLUMN {column} {definition}")
 
         missing_ids = [
             row[0]
             for row in self.conn.execute(
                 "SELECT id FROM events WHERE event_id IS NULL OR event_id = ''"
             ).fetchall()
         ]
         for row_id in missing_ids:
             self.conn.execute(
                 "UPDATE events SET event_id = ? WHERE id = ?",
                 (new_event_id(), row_id),
             )
 
     def append(
         self,
         event_type: str,
         payload: dict[str, Any],
         *,
         event_id: str | None = None,
         workspace_id: str = DEFAULT_WORKSPACE,
         device_id: str = DEFAULT_DEVICE,
     ) -> Event:
         resolved_id = event_id or new_event_id()
         timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
         payload_json = json.dumps(payload)
         with self.conn:
             self.conn.execute(
                 """
                 INSERT OR IGNORE INTO events
                     (event_id, workspace_id, device_id, timestamp, event_type, payload)
                 VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                 """,
                 (resolved_id, workspace_id, device_id, timestamp, event_type, payload_json),
             )
             row = self.conn.execute(
                 """
                 SELECT id, event_id, workspace_id, device_id, timestamp,
                        event_type, payload, server_seq
                 FROM events WHERE event_id = ?
                 """,
                 (resolved_id,),
             ).fetchone()
 
         if row is None:
             raise StoreError(f"event {resolved_id} could not be stored")
         if row[2] != workspace_id:
             raise ConflictError(f"event_id {resolved_id} already belongs to another workspace")
         return self._to_event(row)
 
     def get_stream(
         self,
         *,
         workspace_id: str | None = None,
         after_server_seq: int = 0,
         unsynced_only: bool = False,
         replay_order: bool = False,
     ) -> list[Event]:
         clauses: list[str] = []
         params: list[Any] = []
         if workspace_id is not None:
             clauses.append("workspace_id = ?")
             params.append(workspace_id)
         if after_server_seq:
             clauses.append("server_seq IS NOT NULL AND server_seq > ?")
             params.append(after_server_seq)
         if unsynced_only:
             clauses.append("server_seq IS NULL")
 
         where = f"WHERE {' AND '.join(clauses)}" if clauses else ""
         if replay_order:
             order = "ORDER BY (server_seq IS NULL) ASC, server_seq ASC, id ASC"
         else:
             order = "ORDER BY id ASC"
 
         cursor = self.conn.cursor()
         # `where` and `order` are assembled from the literal fragments above, so
         # interpolating them cannot inject SQL; every caller value is bound.
         sql = (
             "SELECT id, event_id, workspace_id, device_id, timestamp, "
             "event_type, payload, server_seq FROM events "
             f"{where} {order}"  # nosec B608 - static fragments, bound values
         )
         cursor.execute(sql, params)
         return [self._to_event(row) for row in cursor.fetchall()]
 
     @staticmethod
     def _to_event(row: tuple[Any, ...]) -> Event:
         return Event(
             id=row[0],
             event_id=row[1],
             workspace_id=row[2],
             device_id=row[3],
             timestamp=row[4],
             type=row[5],
             payload=json.loads(row[6]) if row[6] else {},
             server_seq=row[7],
         )
 
     def insert_remote(self, events: list[Event]) -> int:
         inserted = 0
         with self.conn:
             for event in events:
                 self.conn.execute(
                     """
                     INSERT OR IGNORE INTO events
                         (event_id, workspace_id, device_id, timestamp,
                          event_type, payload, server_seq)
                     VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                     """,
                     (
                         event["event_id"],
                         event["workspace_id"],
                         event["device_id"],
                         event["timestamp"],
                         event["type"],

                         event.get("server_seq"),
                     ),
                 )
                 self.conn.execute(
                     """
                     UPDATE events SET server_seq = ?
                     WHERE event_id = ? AND server_seq IS NULL AND workspace_id = ?

                     (
                         event.get("server_seq"),
                         event["event_id"],
                         event["workspace_id"],
                     ),
                 )

         updated = 0
         with self.conn:
             for event_id, server_seq in server_seqs.items():
                 cursor = self.conn.execute(
                     "UPDATE events SET server_seq = ? WHERE event_id = ? AND server_seq IS NULL",
                     (server_seq, event_id),
                 )

     def retag_workspace(self, old: str, new: str) -> int:
         updated = 0
